story.logline: A vigilante who falls in love with every unpunished man she sentences drives her latest across the desert, laughing and filming him, still waiting for the dead man to love her back.

beat_sheet.heading: FRONT PAGE · FOR THE READER, BEFORE SC01
beat_sheet.what_happens: Logline: A vigilante who falls in love with every unpunished man she sentences drives her latest across the desert, laughing and filming him, still waiting for the dead man to love her back. Proposition (pending Lucas's approval): punishing the man the system lost can't make him love her back. VENUS finds men whose cases went nowhere, lures each one on a date and kills him. What she wants from every one of them is for him to love her back, and none of them does. Her bar game, decorum, has one rule: she already knows the true answers, so every lie he tells costs him a straw from the house they are building. JEAN (St. Jean, 'just call me J') has dated a lot of beautiful women, and when we meet him he is three nights drunk over a breakup and dressed all in black. His ex's domestic-violence report ended with no charges filed, and his story is that she just left. Tone: a love story played straight, tender in the car and a real flirt at the bar, and in the white apartment the horror is how clean it stays.
beat_sheet.turn: From a woman who can punish any man the system lost to the one thing she can't make happen: a man who loves her back.

beat_sheet.heading: COLD OPEN · EXT. EMPTY DESERT TOWN AND DESERT ROAD, OPEN TWO-SEATER – LATE AFTERNOON TO DUSK (0:00-0:56)
beat_sheet.what_happens: Most of the drive plays inside VENUS's phone: an upright frame with a red REC dot. JEAN rides in the passenger seat of her open two-seater, all in black, cheek on the headrest, head turned to the door. She films him through an empty town and out into open desert, trying to catch him looking back, and she laughs hard enough to shake the picture. He never stirs. At a stop sign nobody else will ever reach, she brushes the dust off his black shirt and straightens his collar. Later her thumb slides to the flip-camera icon, rests there and slides away, and the lens stays on him. The light goes. At dusk she lowers the phone, lifts off his sunglasses and turns his chin toward her with two fingers; his face stays turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. His eyes are open, pale and dusted, and they do not blink. She hooks one arm of the sunglasses into her neckline, raises the phone and laughs. Her thumb rests on the flip icon again, then slides off. She still won't turn the lens on herself.
beat_sheet.turn: From a woman filming her sleeping lover to a woman filming a dead man she still won't step into frame with.

beat_sheet.heading: COLD OPEN · EXT. ABANDONED DESERT MOTEL – LAST LIGHT (0:56-1:12)
beat_sheet.what_happens: Before she brings him in, she needs to know the motel is still hers. VENUS stops in the carport and leans across JEAN's knees, into his open gaze. From the glovebox, where she shut it outside the bar the night before, she takes the pistol and slides it into her back pocket. She walks the frontage alone, tugs the padlock on the office door and checks the dust on its step: unbroken. Only then does she unload his black duffel, her bag and the grocery sacks, and shoulder open the swollen door of a ground-floor room. JEAN stays in the passenger seat, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it; the seat is empty now.
beat_sheet.turn: From arming herself and checking the place to unloading: the motel is still hers.

beat_sheet.heading: COLD OPEN · INT. MOTEL ROOM – NIGHT (1:12-1:30) · LIMERENCE TITLE ON THE FINAL FRAME
beat_sheet.what_happens: By one battery lantern, VENUS's hands set out cans, water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, then pull a second chair up to the table: a table for two. A bedroll on the floor and a row of empty jugs along the far wall show she has been living here for weeks. Above the table is a wall of long-lens photos of JEAN: at a bar window, at a gas pump, crossing a street. He is alone in every one, and none show the two of them together. The frame holds on the table, the two chairs and the wall until nothing moves. LIMERENCE.
beat_sheet.turn: From breaking into a derelict motel to setting a table for two in a room she has lived in for weeks.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. VENUS'S CAR (THE SAME TWO-SEATER, TOP UP), ACROSS FROM A DIVE BAR – THURSDAY NIGHT, THE NIGHT BEFORE (1:30-3:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: The wall was shot from far off, and this is how. Parked across the street, VENUS films JEAN through the bar window. He sits alone at the counter, three nights drunk over a breakup, with a black canvas duffel on the floor under his stool. On her passenger seat are a rubber-banded stack of long-lens prints of him going back months, and a photocopied incident report with a woman's name blacked out and NO CHARGES FILED stamped across it. She zooms in on his face as far as the lens goes. He signals for another. Then the BARTENDER, ready to close him out, sets the tab slip in front of him, and VENUS has minutes before he walks out alone again. She takes the pistol from her back pocket and shuts it in the glovebox, next to a small closed metal tin. She takes the tin and pockets it, sweeps the prints and the report into the glovebox on top of the gun, snaps the side curtain into place and gets out.
beat_sheet.turn: From watching him through a lens to walking into his frame without the gun.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. DIVE BAR – CONTINUOUS (3:00-5:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: She takes the stool beside him and opens with a test she already knows the answer to. VENUS: 'Have we met before?' JEAN: 'No. Not that I'm aware of.' He keeps his eyes on his glass. VENUS: 'Hmm. You seem down. Why don't we play a game?' JEAN: 'Sure.' She lays one straw flat in the wet ring his glass left on the counter. VENUS: 'It's called decorum. The goal is to figure out if the house we build would last. We ask each other questions. Agree, we get a stick. Don't, we take a drink and lose one.' The house is straws laid flat on the counter: four walls and a pitched roof. He stalls by turning it back on her. JEAN: 'Sure we can play, but you haven't gotten your drink yet.' The BARTENDER reaches for the unsigned slip. BARTENDER: 'What can I get you guys?' VENUS: 'How about I get this first round. Two Naked and Famous.' JEAN: 'So what is in a Naked and Famous?' VENUS: 'Something that'll make you famous for being naked.' Her hand lands on his forearm. VENUS: 'Kidding. Mezcal with a touch of personality. Too strong? I can have him change it to a mimosa.' He props himself up. JEAN: 'Ah. Someone with a little character.' He slides the tab slip back to the BARTENDER unsigned. JEAN: 'Let the game begin. Cheers to having some decorum.' VENUS: 'Cheers.'
beat_sheet.turn: From a man drinking to be left alone to a man who pushes back his tab and raises a glass to her game.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. DIVE BAR – LATER (5:30-8:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: The game is a trial he doesn't know he's in. JEAN: 'First question. What is your name, and what do you think it means?' VENUS: 'I was wondering when you'd ask. Venus. Apparently some Roman goddess of love. What about you?' JEAN: 'St. Jean. But just call me J, it's easier.' VENUS: 'I've met a saint. The Lord has answered my prayers. I think we just earned a stick toward our home.' She lays a second straw flat against the first: a wall. VENUS: 'Why do you look so defeated?' JEAN: 'Damn, I'm that easily read. You see it in my eye or my face?' VENUS: 'I felt it in your soul. Damaged, like you'd just been slayed.' She laughs. VENUS: 'A true martyr on a Thursday night, alone in an empty bar. Who slayed you, my friend?' JEAN: 'She left. Packed while I was at work. I never once raised my voice.' Nobody asked about his voice, and his own packed duffel sits at his feet. VENUS drinks and pulls the wall straw back out. JEAN: 'That's a no?' VENUS: 'That's a drink.' She closes the gap between the stools and leans to his ear. VENUS: 'Why do they call you a saint? Are you willing to save me?' She pulls back, laughing. VENUS: 'I'm just fucking with you. My turn.'
beat_sheet.turn: From a straw earned to a straw taken: her first verdict, which he hears as flirting.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. DIVE BAR – CONTINUOUS, BY THE CANDLE (8:00-9:45)
beat_sheet.what_happens: JEAN takes her turn before she can use it and slides the bar candle between them so he can see her eyes. JEAN: 'Let's go deeper.' VENUS: 'Sure. My heart's an open book, if you want to read it.' JEAN: 'What makes you tingle inside?' VENUS: 'Ahh. Good one.' She holds his eyes. VENUS: 'A man who doesn't have any fear and is willing to tame a beast.' JEAN: 'What dog doesn't want a true owner?' He picks up a straw and, instead of laying it flat, stands it upright in the candle's soft wax: a chimney he awards himself. Her fingertip rests on top of it, the way it rested on the wall straw before she pulled it, then slides away, and the chimney stays standing. VENUS: 'Who would have known a stranger could be my next lover?' For three seconds she is somewhere else: her hand on a black shirt against white sheets. She shakes her head and is back at the bar.
beat_sheet.turn: From judge to lover: her fingertip leaves standing a straw she should have pulled.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT./EXT. DIVE BAR, THROUGH THE WINDOW, THEN THE STREET – LAST CALL (9:45-11:00) · END OF ACT ONE
beat_sheet.what_happens: Through the window, with no sound and cut on the laughs, the flat house grows when he adds a straw and shrinks when she pulls one, while the chimney stands in the candle wax beside it. Once it has its whole roof. He sets his fresh coupe down on the base straw; it rocks; he lifts it off, laughing. On the next drink her fingertip draws a roof straw out of the line, and he laughs again. Inside at last call the counter is bare except for the chimney, upright in the candle wax: the only straw still standing. JEAN holds his phone out at arm's length to fit the two of them and the chimney in one frame. VENUS takes the phone from his hand, photographs him alone beside the upright straw and hands it back without a word. The BARTENDER reaches to clear the glasses. JEAN reaches for the chimney to take home as a trophy. VENUS plucks it first and slides it into her jacket pocket beside the tin. He shoulders his duffel. They walk out with their arms tangled, leaving her two-seater parked across the street.
beat_sheet.turn: From his phone framing the two of them to a photo of him alone and the last straw in her pocket: she has him, and the verdict is still open.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · EXT. BAR CURB, THEN INT. RIDESHARE BACK SEAT – NIGHT, DASH CAM (11:00-12:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: At the curb JEAN books the ride on his own phone, and VENUS leans in and types the drop-off herself: a corner, not a door. In the back seat she takes the seat directly behind the DRIVER. The dash cam's frame, a date and timestamp running in its corner, holds JEAN's face, her hands on his jaw and the back of her head as they kiss and grab at each other with their clothes on, his duffel on the floor at their feet. The DRIVER flicks the dome light on and watches them in the mirror. VENUS reaches up and flicks it off, and the dash cam frame drops to grain and passing streetlight. JEAN's hands go inside her jacket and find the pocket with the tin and the straw. She takes his wrist and moves his hand to her waist, laughing against his mouth, her face still turned from the lens. The car stops at a corner a block from her building, and they get out.
beat_sheet.turn: From a lit cab with a camera on them and his hand on the tin to the light off and his hand at her waist: the camera keeps his face and never hers, and the tin stays shut.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. VENUS'S BUILDING, LOBBY AND STAIRS TO HER DOOR – NIGHT (12:30-14:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: JEAN takes in the marble lobby and the quiet stairwell, and the questions start: who is she, and how does she pay for this? JEAN: 'So what do you-' VENUS: 'Mind the step.' He lets it go. She climbs a step ahead of him. VENUS: 'Please don't judge me. It's a little messy.' JEAN: 'We aren't all perfect. Who said Rome was built in a day?' She opens the door on an all-white apartment: white floor, white furniture, no dust anywhere. He stands on the threshold in all black. She lines his black shoes up on the white mat by the door and sets his duffel beside them. JEAN: 'I happened to miss the mess. Can I use your bathroom?' VENUS: 'Of course. Right on the left. I'm gonna change and make us something to drink.'
beat_sheet.turn: From a man with questions to a man who stops asking and walks in.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BATHROOM – NIGHT (14:00-15:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: JEAN grins at himself in the mirror and checks his teeth, in a hurry to get back out to her. He lifts the white toilet seat and finds a few small dried red drops on the back of the rim, left by the man before him. He tears off toilet paper and wets it under the tap. Through the door, a trance-soul track starts low, under the ice dropping into glasses. He wipes, looks at the faint pink on the tissue, drops it in the bowl and flushes. He walks out smiling.
beat_sheet.turn: From a man who finds blood to a man who wipes it away and walks out smiling.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BEDROOM TO LIVING ROOM – NIGHT, SAME TIME AS SC11 (15:00-17:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: While the tap runs behind the bathroom door, VENUS, changed into an oversized team T-shirt, bare legs, turns the dial on the small white speaker on her bedroom nightstand, beside her phone. A trance-soul track starts low. She drops ice into two glasses, pours, carries them to the white table and squares them side by side; once the track fills the room, her hands go still on them. The chimney straw from the bar stands upright in the ice of her own glass. The bathroom door opens, and she lifts both glasses and turns to him, one in each hand. JEAN: 'Did you miss me?' VENUS: 'You haven't shown me anything worth missing.' He takes the other glass, downs it like a shot and blows out hard. JEAN: 'Whew!' VENUS: 'You alright, champ?' JEAN: 'I ain't won a ring yet.' His hand goes to her waist and steers her toward the bedroom door. She sets her glass on the white table, the straw still standing, and slides a small metal tin across to him, closed. He turns it over like a prize and tries the lid, but her fingertip stays on it. VENUS: 'Let's take a trip.' JEAN: 'Like the one where we get on a plane, or the one where we have a good time?' VENUS: 'Both. You feel like this space isn't safe?' JEAN: 'No. Not at all.'
beat_sheet.turn: From a drink he can swallow to a tin he can't open: the last straw stands again, in her glass.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, LIVING ROOM – CONTINUOUS (17:00-20:00) · END OF ACT TWO
beat_sheet.what_happens: The last question is his last straw. VENUS: 'Trust is a thing that is earned. You can't assume things are great. What's glamorous can be a trap for a black hole. Do you think love is built on trust or lust? What makes one lust, the words or the sex appeal?' He inches closer and puts his hand on her thigh. JEAN: 'Hmm.' VENUS: 'Who is to say love has a conditional standard? Who is to say lust doesn't have great intentions? Who created the standard of what's wrong or right?' He reaches for a comeback. JEAN: 'Why does love have to be right or wrong? Why does pain have to be felt? Words have made me stronger, yet pain has made me hopeless. Everyone's standard must belong to who they are within.' VENUS: 'How does that correlate to love, or what I just asked?' JEAN: 'That's for you to find out.' She draws the straw out of her ice and lays it flat on the white table, where it leaves a wet mark. She lifts her fingertip off the tin and opens the lid toward him. What's inside stays out of frame.
beat_sheet.turn: From a straw standing in her ice to a straw lying flat and the tin open: he gave her a line, and the house is down.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, HALL TO BEDROOM – NIGHT (20:00-21:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: JEAN lifts VENUS and carries her toward the bedroom, past the open tin and the flat straw on the table. At the white threshold he looks down at three small dried red drops on the floor and stops for half a step. She never looks down. She turns his face back to hers. VENUS: 'J.' He steps over the drops and carries her through.
beat_sheet.turn: From stopping at the drops to stepping over them.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BEDROOM AND BATHROOM – LATER THAT NIGHT (21:30-24:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: Afterwards JEAN sleeps face-down in the white sheets, breathing slow and loud, his black clothes on the white floor. The track still plays low from the small white speaker on the nightstand, beside her phone. VENUS folds his black clothes square on a white chair. In the bathroom she runs the tap and washes her hands at the basin, eyes down, never meeting the mirror; the cabinet stays shut. His breathing carries through the open door. She lies down beside him. His breathing stops for a long gap, then catches with a rasp. Her hand passes the phone and turns the speaker's dial up until his breathing is under the music.
beat_sheet.turn: From a breath that catches while he could still be helped to the dial turned up over it: she reaches past her phone and stays in bed.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BEDROOM – MORNING (24:00-25:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: The track is still looping the same four bars. JEAN lies face-down, mouth open, one arm off the bed, as he has lain since the night. VENUS lies awake beside him, a hand pressed to her forehead, waiting for him to turn over and reach for her. She waits through another loop. She lifts his arm over her waist, and it slides off. VENUS: 'J. Stay for breakfast.' He doesn't answer. She rolls him onto his back herself; his open eyes face the ceiling. With one hand she turns his face toward her on the pillow, and it stays where she sets it. She reaches over and switches the speaker off. In the silence she sits up and pulls the fitted corner off her side of the mattress.
beat_sheet.turn: From waiting for him to turn over to turning him herself and pulling the first corner off the bed.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. REAR SERVICE BAY, THEN WHITE APARTMENT – MORNING, CONTINUOUS (25:30-28:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: Four silent seconds downstairs, in the building's enclosed rear service bay: the roller door is down, the service lift's doors stand open, and the two-seater waits beside them, top down, its passenger seat empty, the only light from a high window. Upstairs, VENUS dresses JEAN in his black clothes, seats him in the white armchair and puts his sunglasses on him. She zips his duffel and stands it by the door. She pulls the rest of the sheets off and remakes the bed in fresh white, pulling the corners tight and smoothing until no crease is left. In the bathroom she wipes the cabinet shelf and lifts the four-week pill organizer, every compartment still full, a pharmacy fill slip taped inside its lid dated five weeks before the dash cam's date (on screen: the date only). She wipes under it and sets it back square beside an amber vial, its label turned to the wall. At the bedroom threshold she finds the three dried drops JEAN stepped over, which she had missed. She kneels and scrubs until the white cloth is pink and the floor is white, then folds the pink cloth into a square and drops it in the trash. From the white table she takes the flat straw and drops it in on top of the cloth. She closes the tin and pockets only that. The frame holds on the finished room, JEAN in black in the white chair, longer than is comfortable.
beat_sheet.turn: From a room she thought was clean to a flaw she missed and scrubs out: spotless, with nothing of him kept and a dead man in black at its center.

beat_sheet.heading: TAG · INT. MOTEL ROOM – NIGHT, CONTINUOUS FROM THE COLD OPEN (28:00-30:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: Back at the motel, JEAN sits in the second chair at the table under his wall, lantern and oranges in front of him, his face still turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it: at the table, that is his left. VENUS unhooks his sunglasses from her neckline and sets them by the oranges. From her bag she takes two long-lens prints of a different man on courthouse steps and pins them at the edge of the wall, next to the last photos of JEAN. She pulls her chair to his right, the side his face is turned away from, rests her head on his right shoulder and raises her phone at arm's length in front of them, a little to her right. Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon, and this time it presses. The screen shows both of them: her face in the lantern light, smiling into the lens; beside it, his face in three-quarter, his open eyes aimed off to his left, past the lens. Two of her fingers lift toward his chin, then stop. She takes the photo anyway. The palm-sized printer whirs, the only sound in the room, and she pins the print between JEAN's photos and the new man's: the only photo of them together.
beat_sheet.turn: From never being in his frame to being in it, while the wall already moves on to the next man.

beat_sheet.heading: SEASON ENGINE · ONE PAGE AFTER THE PILOT
beat_sheet.what_happens: The season question: what happens when a man tells the truth at decorum and seems to love her back, and can she still sentence him? Every episode opens on her phone recording the next man the system let walk. Every episode closes at the motel table with the one photograph she lets herself take with each of them, afterwards. Each week brings a new man, a new round of decorum and a new wall, and each straw house stands a little longer before she pulls the last straw. The man on the courthouse steps, pinned up in the pilot's last scene, is episode two. At midseason one man answers her last question with one true thing. His house stands, and she turns the front camera on while he is still alive. The finale asks whether she can open the tin for him.
beat_sheet.turn: From a woman who is only ever photographed beside dead men to the one man she could photograph alive.

deliverable_scripts.idea_in_one_line: She laughs and films a sleeping man across the desert until his open eyes show he is dead, then sets a table for two under a wall of his photos, none of them together.

beats.picture: Inside her phone's upright frame, centered in black: JEAN sits in the passenger seat of an open two-seater, cheek on the headrest, head turned to the door, so only his black collar, jaw and one arm of his sunglasses show. Low gold sun; the edge of an empty town slides by behind him. The picture jolts when she laughs.
beats.sound: Wind clipping the phone mic. VENUS's laugh, loud and right on the mic. No score.

beats.picture: Phone frame. The car rolls to a full stop at a stop sign on an empty crossroads, with no other car in any direction and the sign behind his head. VENUS's free hand enters the frame, brushes dust off his black shirt and straightens his collar. He doesn't stir. The frame lurches as she drives on. [Fallback: her hand only rests on his collar.]
beats.sound: The engine idling, the wind dropped to nothing, her fingers brushing fabric close to the mic, then the engine pulling away.

beats.picture: Three jump cuts inside the phone frame, the timer jumping at each: empty storefronts, then open desert, then scrub hills pass behind JEAN, with the gold sun lower every time. His head, collar and sunglasses never move between cuts.
beats.sound: The wind roar cut hard three times, each cut landing on a different snatch of her laugh.

beats.picture: Phone frame, the sun low behind the car. Her thumb slides across the glass to the flip-camera icon in the corner, rests on it, then slides away. The lens stays on JEAN's turned head, and the frame shakes as she laughs. [Fallback: the screen flips to the front camera for under a second and catches both of them, her face cut off by the top edge, his head slumped against the door, sunglasses crooked; then it flips back to him.]
beats.sound: Wind on the mic. Her laugh, shorter.

beats.picture: Blue dusk inside the phone frame. From here the phone records without a break until it rises again at 52 s. The phone's small video light switches on and hits JEAN's black collar, and the fine desert dust on the fabric glints. His head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: The wind easing on the mic; tires on grit underneath.

beats.picture: For the first 0.8 s (19 frames) the upright phone frame still holds JEAN's turned head, and the timer runs on from REC 01:04:37, shown on these frames only. Then she lowers the phone to her lap and the picture opens to full width, film grain replacing the phone's compression: the open two-seater alone on the dusk road, VENUS laughing at the wheel with her eyes on JEAN, whose head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: For 0.8 s, wind on the phone mic. Then the wind drops away: tires and engine heard from outside the car, her laugh further off.

beats.picture: Full width, the car still moving. VENUS lifts the sunglasses off JEAN's face and, still holding them, turns his chin toward her with two fingers; his face stays turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. His eyes are open, pale and dusted. The wind moves his hair, and they do not blink. [Fallback, A16: the same action with the car parked at the motel.]
beats.sound: Tires and engine. No laugh.

beats.picture: In the first second she hooks one open arm of the sunglasses into her neckline. At 52 s she raises the phone from the driver's seat and the picture narrows back to the upright frame, with the timer showing again from that moment. JEAN's open eyes sit frontal and centered under the video light, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. The frame shakes as she laughs. Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon, rests there, then slides back. [Fallback: the front camera for under a second, her face lit by the video light beside his open eyes, which look past the lens; then it flips back to him.]
beats.sound: The wind comes back on the mic. Her laugh, softer and close.

beats.picture: Full width, last light. The two-seater stands in the carport of an abandoned motel under a peeling MOTEL sign on steel legs, JEAN in the passenger seat, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. VENUS leans across his knees, into his open gaze, opens the glovebox, takes out a pistol and slides it into her back pocket. [Fallback: the pistol already in her back pocket, no hand on it.]
beats.sound: The cooling engine pinging, the glovebox latch dropping open, wind in dry palms.

beats.picture: Full width: VENUS walks the gutted motel frontage alone, the pistol grip showing from her back pocket. She tugs the padlock on the office door and looks down at the unbroken dust on its step.
beats.sound: Gravel under her boots, a loose panel on the sign ticking in the wind, the padlock knocking on its hasp.

beats.picture: At the car, VENUS lifts out his black bag, her own bag and two paper grocery sacks. JEAN stays in the passenger seat, his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it; the seat is empty now. She carries the bags to a ground-floor room and shoulders its swollen door open.
beats.sound: The trunk lid, paper sacks rustling, the door scraping open over grit.

beats.picture: Inside the room: one battery lantern on a wooden table, a bedroll on the floor and a row of empty water jugs along the far wall. Her hands set down cans, full water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, then pull a second chair up to the table. On the wall above are dozens of long-lens photos of JEAN, alone in every one; none show the two of them together.
beats.sound: The lantern switch clicking, cans set down on wood, a chair leg dragging across the boards.

beats.picture: A held frame in which nothing moves: the lantern, the oranges, the cans, the printer, two empty chairs, the bedroll and the row of empty jugs along the far wall. Above the table is the wall of JEAN photos, none of which include her.
beats.sound: Only the wind outside, pushing at the door.

beats.picture: The same held frame of the lantern-lit table, the two empty chairs, the bedroll and the wall of JEAN photos, with the LIMERENCE title card landing over it.
beats.sound: Silence.

deliverable_scripts.idea_in_one_line: Her phone keeps recording a man who never wakes; his open eyes show why, and her thumb won't turn the camera on herself.

beats.picture: The upright phone frame fills the screen. Stopped at the stop sign, VENUS's hand brushes dust off JEAN's black shirt and straightens his collar while his head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: Wind on the mic, fabric under her fingers.

beats.picture: Hard cut to the same pose inside the phone frame: JEAN's collar, jaw and sunglasses haven't moved, the open desert is behind him and the gold sun is much lower.
beats.sound: A burst of wind and a snatch of her laugh.

beats.picture: Blue dusk, the full-width shot reframed upright. VENUS lifts the sunglasses off JEAN's face and turns his chin toward her with two fingers, the dusk road behind them.
beats.sound: Tires on grit and the engine, heard from outside the car.

beats.picture: Phone frame under the small video light: JEAN's eyes, open, pale and dusted, fill the frame. The wind moves his hair, and they do not blink.
beats.sound: Wind on the mic.

beats.picture: Her laugh shakes the phone frame from side to side while JEAN's open eyes stay centered in it, unblinking, the timer still running.
beats.sound: Her laugh, soft and close to the mic.

beats.picture: Her thumb slides onto the flip-camera icon in the corner of the frame, rests there over his open eyes, then slides back off. [Fallback: the under-a-second flip to both of them, then back to him.]
beats.sound: Wind, then the mic cuts out.

beats.picture: The recording stops: the upright frame goes black, the red REC dot is gone, and the LIMERENCE title card sits centered in the dark.
beats.sound: Silence.

stills_copy.picture: Key art, 2:3, 35mm film look. Shot from behind VENUS's right shoulder at the wheel of the open two-seater in low gold sun. She laughs in three-quarter profile, and her raised phone shows JEAN under a red REC dot. Beside the phone the real JEAN sits pale and still in his black shirt, sunglasses on, head turned to the door. Two of him, none of her.
stills_copy.headline: LIMERENCE

stills_copy.picture: World frame, 16:9, 35mm film look. The motel room by one battery lantern: a wall of dozens of long-lens photos of JEAN, alone in every one, none of them together. Below the wall is a table set with cans, water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, with two chairs pulled up. A bedroll lies on the floor and a row of empty water jugs stands along the far wall.

Social frame, 4:5, 35mm film look. A dim bar counter by candlelight. Between two cocktail glasses, drinking straws lie flat on the wood in the outline of a house, four walls and a pitched roof, with one wall straw in a wet ring. Beside the house, one straw stands upright in the soft wax of the bar candle: the chimney. VENUS's fingertip draws one roof straw out of the line.

decisions.choice: Jean's head after the chin turn has one position, written in the same words everywhere: 'his face turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it'. The phrase is used in V01-B07, B08, B09 and B11, SC01 and SC02. In SC18, at the motel table, the same position is his left, and she sits at his right. Before the reveal the phrase is 'head turned to the door' (V01-B01 to B06, V02-B01/B02, S01). The rule behind it: after death his head moves only when her hand moves it, stays where she sets it, and never lolls or bobs. In story order her hand first sets it in SC16, on the pillow. Correction: the previous version said B09, B11, SC02 and SC18 already matched, but they read 'still set toward the windshield'. That claim was wrong, and the text is now fixed.
decisions.reason: In B08 she films from the driver's seat, so his open eyes sit frontal in her phone, and the make-or-break shot (A16) depends on that. In B09 she leans across his knees straight into his gaze. In SC18 his eyes are turned to his left while she sits on his right, so they aim past the lens because of where people sit, and the page doesn't have to say so.
decisions.source: Reviewer note (continuity that holds); A16; taste note (hands before faces)

decisions.choice: Logged as deliberate stylization, not physiology: the dusk chin turn in V01-B07 comes about 18 hours after Jean dies in the night, when a real body would be rigid, and his face at 42 s is pale. Both stay as written. SC16 has her roll him onto his back in the morning, so the pilot no longer leaves him face-down all day against the pale face at 42 s.
decisions.reason: True-crime followers will do this arithmetic. Naming it as a stylization, the same way the SC17 service bay is logged, tells every department it is a choice and not a mistake, and keeps anyone from fixing it with medical detail on screen.
decisions.source: Reviewer note (SC16); brief audience; A16

decisions.choice: SC16 now turns inside the scene. After his arm slides off her waist and 'J. Stay for breakfast.' gets no answer, she rolls him onto his back herself and turns his face toward her on the pillow, where it stays. She switches the speaker off, sits up and pulls the fitted corner off her side of the mattress: the first visible sign of the bed being stripped. SC17 opens with her pulling off the rest of the sheets.
decisions.reason: Ref 06's 'waiting for him to turn over', as the brief describes it, is answered by her doing it for him. The scene ends on the turn's first visible consequence and not on a silence.
decisions.source: Craft brief ('Every scene turns, and the turn is visible'; 'end on the turn or its first visible consequence'); must-include (the morning after); reviewer note

decisions.choice: SC09 keeps Lucas's dash-cam shot and makes the dash cam the one camera she keeps her face out of. At the curb JEAN books the ride on his own phone, and she types the drop-off: a corner a block from her building. She takes the seat directly behind the DRIVER, so the timestamped frame holds JEAN's face, her hands on his jaw and the back of her head, never her face. Flicking the dome light off darkens the lens as well as the driver's mirror. No in-world camera holds her face until the front camera in SC18.
decisions.reason: It answers the true-crime viewer's first question, the ride record and the footage from the night he vanished, just as the SC17 bay answers the second (how he left the building). It also extends R2: she is never in his frame until the photograph.
decisions.source: Route R2 central idea; brief audience; reviewer note; the SC17 service-bay decision

decisions.choice: The trance-soul track is source only, SC11-SC16. It plays from a small white speaker with a physical dial on her bedroom nightstand, beside her phone. SC11: heard through the bathroom door under the ice dropping into glasses. SC12: she starts it low while JEAN is in the bathroom, and her hands, squaring the two glasses, go still once it plays. SC15: her hand passes the phone and turns the dial up until his breathing is under the music. SC16: she switches it off. Every other scene carries its own sound. Bent on purpose: the taste note says music comes in late, if at all, but here it enters at about 14 minutes, mid-pilot.
decisions.reason: The climax in SC15 needs the track planted a scene ahead. The brief says it plays to quiet her, and SC12 shows that in her hands. The dial answers how she plays it without touching her phone. The music stays inside the scene, and V01, V02 and the stills have none.
decisions.source: Craft brief (plant what the climax needs); tone (music); A08; verified fact (trance-soul music to quiet her); taste note (sound design before music: bent, flagged)

decisions.choice: The meds appear only in SC17's clean-up, after the death. She wipes the cabinet shelf and lifts the four-week pill organizer: every compartment is still full, and a pharmacy fill slip taped inside its lid is dated five weeks before the dash cam's date (on screen, the date only). She wipes under it and squares it with the amber vial, whose label is turned to the wall. In SC15 her tactic is to wash her hands at the basin without meeting the mirror, and the cabinet stays shut.
decisions.reason: A full organizer on its own reads as freshly filled. The dated slip makes 'untaken for weeks' visible on camera without naming a drug. Putting them after the death keeps them seen and never the reason.
decisions.source: Must-include (meds untaken for weeks); verified facts (meds in her bathroom; untaken for weeks); must avoid (meds as the explanation); reviewer note

decisions.choice: The straw chain. The house lies flat on the counter as four walls and a pitched roof. Jean's own straw stands upright in the candle wax as the chimney (SC07). It is the only straw left at last call and goes into her pocket (SC08), stands in her ice (SC12) and is laid flat on the white table before the tin opens (SC13). In SC17 she drops the flat straw into the trash on top of the folded pink cloth and pockets only the tin. S03 now shows the chimney upright in the candle wax beside the flat house as her fingertip draws out a roof straw.
decisions.reason: She isn't collecting trophies. The SC18 photograph is the only thing she keeps of him, against Jean's own wish in SC08 to take the chimney home as a trophy. The chimney is the detail that makes S03 belong to this show and not to any bar game. The tin opens only after his line (A18).
decisions.source: Route R2 central idea; brief S03; A04; A18; craft brief (an object that comes back meaning something else); reviewer note

decisions.choice: D01 is written for execs. It opens with a FRONT page (logline; the proposition, pending Lucas; Venus in three sentences; Jean in two; tone in one). Every scene is present-tense story prose, with no 'X wants' labels. The wants, tactics, details and production notes live in the crew annex below.
decisions.reason: The exec decides at D01, straight after V01, and should be reading a story, not a template.
decisions.source: Package review notes; strategy desired behavior

decisions.choice: SC17 opens with a 4 s silent insert in the building's enclosed rear service bay: roller door down, the service lift's doors open, the two-seater beside them with the top down and the passenger seat empty, the only light from a high window. This is logged as a convenience of the world, like the stylization above.
decisions.reason: True-crime followers will ask how she moved a dead man from a second-floor flat into an open car in daylight. A private bay beside a service lift answers that without showing the move.
decisions.source: Package review notes (world bible LOC-07); brief audience

decisions.choice: SC04: she sweeps the prints and the incident report into the glovebox on top of the gun and snaps the side curtain into place before she crosses to the bar. The report's stamp reads NO CHARGES FILED.
decisions.reason: Nothing incriminating is left on an open seat overnight, and the wording matches the US Southwest setting.
decisions.source: Package review notes (PR-09)

decisions.choice: Two physical beats: in SC08's silent window montage he sets his fresh coupe down on the base straw, it rocks and he lifts it off, laughing; in SC11 he wets the tissue under the tap before he wipes.
decisions.reason: The coupe re-wets the base straw's ring, so S03's wet ring is physically true. Dried drops on glazed china only come off pink with a damp tissue.
decisions.source: Package review notes (PR-32, PR-48); brief S03

decisions.choice: US vocabulary and spelling throughout (windshield, curb, trunk, tires, organizer, centered). The empty water jugs stand 'along the far wall' in SC03, V01-B12, B13 and S02.
decisions.reason: Every department reads one vocabulary, and the jugs sit where the held frame can see them.
decisions.source: Package review notes (PR-23)

decisions.choice: Crew annex, SC01-SC06. SC01 (V01 0-56 s): VENUS wants to film JEAN looking back at her. JEAN, dead, wants nothing, and his stillness is the obstacle. Her tactics: film him close, fix his collar at the stop sign, move her thumb to the flip icon. Detail: the stop sign nobody else will reach. From B07 on, his face stays turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it. SC02 (V01 56-72 s): VENUS wants proof nobody has found the motel. Detail: the unbroken dust on the office step. The pistol comes from the glovebox (the SC04 chain). SC03 (V01 72-90 s): VENUS wants the table set for two. The printer and the second chair plant SC18. SC04: VENUS wants to get in before he leaves alone again; the BARTENDER wants to close him out. Detail: the gun traded for the tin. The report and every case are fictional. The duffel plants V01-B11. SC05: VENUS wants him to agree to play; JEAN wants to finish his drink unseen; the BARTENDER wants the order in and the tab closed. Her tactics: the test question, the joke, the hand on his forearm, the mimosa dare; his is the stall. Detail: the first straw in the wet ring. The inciting incident lands at about 3:00. SC06: JEAN wants to be the wronged man in her eyes; VENUS wants the truth about his ex. His flaw under pressure: he lies to stay the wronged man. Detail: his denial of what nobody asked, with the packed duffel at his feet (A02, A04).
decisions.reason: The crew keeps every want, tactic and note that stays out of the exec text.
decisions.source: Previous crew annex; reviewer notes

decisions.choice: Crew annex, SC07-SC12. SC07: JEAN wants to take her home tonight; VENUS wants a reason to let him pass. Detail: the chimney straw in the wax. The white-sheets insert runs at real speed, with no nudity. SC08: JEAN wants a picture of the night, then the chimney as a trophy; VENUS wants him out the door with the verdict still hers; the BARTENDER wants the counter cleared. The roof straw pulled, with the chimney in the wax beside it, is the S03 frame. SC09: JEAN wants his hands inside her jacket; the DRIVER wants his back seat kept clean; VENUS wants the tin kept hers and her face out of the dash cam. The ride is on his phone to a corner, not a door; she sits directly behind the driver. The rideshare is unmarked (A10). Detail: the dash cam, the one camera she keeps her face out of. SC10: JEAN wants to know who she is and how she pays for this, but wants the night more; VENUS wants him inside without questions. Detail: his shoes and duffel on the white mat. SC11: JEAN wants to get back out to her fast. The drops belong to the previous man (A13) and are never explained on screen. The track is heard through the door. SC12: VENUS wants to quiet herself before he comes out, then the last question first; JEAN wants her in the bedroom now. The speaker, with a physical dial, sits on the bedroom nightstand beside her phone. The team shirt carries no logo (A10). Detail: her hands going still on the squared glasses; the straw standing in her ice.
decisions.reason: The crew keeps every want, tactic and note that stays out of the exec text.
decisions.source: Previous crew annex; reviewer notes; must avoid (brands, explicit sex)

decisions.choice: Crew annex, SC13-SC18. SC13: VENUS wants one true thing about love, his last straw; JEAN wants her in the bedroom. Detail: the wet mark on the white table. The tin's contents stay out of frame. SC14: JEAN wants her in the bed; VENUS wants him to keep walking. Detail: the drops at the threshold, where she never looks. SC15: VENUS wants to stop hearing his breathing. Her tactics: fold his clothes, wash her hands without meeting the mirror, turn the speaker's dial up. The breath catch is her climactic choice. No meds appear. SC16: VENUS wants him to turn over and reach for her. Her tactics: wait, lift his arm, say the line, then roll him over herself. Details: the four-bar loop; the fitted corner. The performance rule starts here, with his face on the pillow where her hand sets it. SC17: VENUS wants the apartment spotless before she takes JEAN away, with nothing of him kept. The meds: organizer full, fill slip in the lid dated five weeks before the dash cam's date, the vial's label to the wall, no drug name or diagnosis (PR-50, PR-51). The flat straw goes into the trash on top of the pink cloth; only the tin goes into her pocket. The sunglasses plant V01-B07. Detail: the pink cloth folded square. SC18: VENUS wants to get into one photograph with JEAN. She sits at his right, the side his face is turned away from, with the phone in front of them and a little to her right, so his eyes, turned to his left, miss the lens. Her fingers stop short of his chin. Detail: the printer's whir. The courthouse-steps prints show a fictional man.
decisions.reason: The crew keeps every want, tactic and note that stays out of the exec text.
decisions.source: Previous crew annex; reviewer notes; must avoid (the tin's contents; meds as the explanation; real cases)

decisions.choice: The whole piece is written for a 35mm film look. Her phone's upright frame keeps its compression, fingerprint smear and UI, and when she lowers the phone (V01-B06) the picture goes from phone video to film grain. The stills carry the same look. Stock, grain, gate, lenses and grade belong to the camera department.
decisions.reason: Where Lucas's relayed request and the route differ, his request wins, and it sharpens the route's rule that sets her phone against the world as it is.
decisions.source: Relayed user request ('35mm film style'); route R2 visual language

decisions.choice: The V01 REC clock runs without contradiction. The phone records without a break from 26.0 s to 52.0 s: B05 reads REC 01:04:29; B06's first 0.8 s (19 upright frames) shows REC 01:04:37, and the timer is hidden once the frame widens; from 52.0 s, B08 reads REC 01:04:55. The cut from B04 (00:53:10) to B05 is the only time jump.
decisions.reason: With 26 s of recording between 26.0 s and 52.0 s, the timer lands on its own number inside one continuous take.
decisions.source: Package review (storyboard flag 3; camera plan SH09-SH16)

decisions.choice: V02 runs on a teaser clock that is deliberately not frame-matched to V01: B01 reads 00:06:13, and B04-B06 read 01:04:55, 01:04:58 and 01:05:00.
decisions.reason: The teaser has 15 s to carry an hour's drive and the reveal. It keeps V01's timer language without claiming V01's continuity.
decisions.source: Brief V02 ('rebuilt from V01 footage')

evidence.specificity: All four departments can break it down without a follow-up call. Design gets dated objects: SC17 'lifts the four-week pill organizer, every compartment still full, a pharmacy fill slip taped inside its lid dated five weeks before the dash cam's date (on screen: the date only)'. Sound gets an action it can play: SC15 'Her hand passes the phone and turns the speaker's dial up until his breathing is under the music.' Every V01 beat has its own sound, for example B10 'the padlock knocking on its hasp'. The blocking is written down: SC18 'She pulls her chair to his right, the side his face is turned away from'. The one thing that stops a 10 is that a few beats pack in more hand action than their seconds can hold (see notes). That is a craft problem, not a gap in specificity.
evidence.distinctiveness: Every device is this show's own. SC07 'stands it upright in the candle's soft wax: a chimney he awards himself'. SC08 'VENUS takes the phone from his hand, photographs him alone beside the upright straw and hands it back without a word.' SC09 'In the back seat she takes the seat directly behind the DRIVER.' SC18 'Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon, and this time it presses.' S03 now includes the chimney, which ties the still to this story rather than to any bar game. Drop any of these into another vigilante pilot and it stops making sense.

characters.role_in_story: Principal. A vigilante who watches unpunished men for months, then plays decorum with them over a date. She films everything and is never in her own frame. V01 objective: get JEAN to look back at her through her phone. Pilot want: one true thing about love from him, then one photograph with him. Obstacle: he is the man she is sentencing, he answers with lines, and by the cold open he is dead. Change: from never being in his frame to the first photo of them together (SC18), while the wall moves on to the next man. Age 30-38, target 34. Every face reads 30+ at the bar (alcohol, no market code given), and she is old enough to have kept a wall for months and paid for the white apartment. Defaults: I keep Lucas's height, slimness and long brown hair with highlights. I break the genre default (a glossy femme fatale in her late 20s) and the generator's stock face (symmetrical, poreless, smiling at the lens) with pores, laugh lines, one higher brow and marked working hands. She smiles at him, never at us, until SC18. Heritage: Black American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. It is a casting choice, not a story need, and Lucas approves it (see blockers).
characters.screen_presence: In one frame (in the left-hand-drive car the script now places): a woman in her mid-thirties, left hand on the wheel, right hand holding a phone out toward the man on her right. Her shoulders are loose and her eyes are on him, not the road. The read: in love, not driving. Her hands lead (taste note: hands before faces). At the stop sign her left hand crosses to his collar, brushes the dust off and straightens it. Her right thumb rests on the flip icon, then slides away. At the motel she leans across his knees into his open gaze and doesn't look away. She handles things slowly, and whatever she puts down lands square: cans, his shoes on the white mat, the two glasses, his folded clothes, the pink cloth. Between actions she is still and watching. She laughs with her whole torso, so the phone shakes. At the bar she sits turned fully to him, elbows off the counter, one fingertip on the straws. In the rideshare she keeps the back of her head to the dash cam, even while laughing against his mouth. In SC14 she never looks down at the drops. In SC17 she finds them herself.
characters.performance_style: Naturalistic, played as a love story. The laugh is the only heightened thing: real, from the belly, never a cackle. One laugh voice is locked across V01, V02 and D01: low, breaking high at the end, with no words. It syncs to her face only at 34-42 s and in the front-camera fallbacks, and it softens after the eyes (V01-B08). At rest her face stays pleasant and busy with him: no knowing glance, no half-closed stare, no lip bite (taste note: restraint over explanation). At the bar she blinks less than he does. Beside the dead JEAN she blinks normally, so in a shared frame her blink is the one difference between them. Lens rule: her eyes never go into any lens, including the under-a-second flips in the V01-B04 and B08 fallbacks, where they stay on him. The first time is SC18, into her own front camera. D01 is sync dialogue, dry and quick. She plays the flirt as genuine because she hopes he will pass (A18), and her verdicts land with no change of face ('That's a drink'). Repeated gesture: a digit rests, then slides off. Her right thumb does it on the flip icon, and her fingertip does it on the chimney straw (SC07) and on the tin's lid until his line (SC12-SC13). SC15: she washes her hands without meeting the mirror. When his breath stops and rasps, her hand passes the phone without resting on it and turns the dial up at the pace she fixed his collar, with no change of face. SC16 opens as the one stretch where her hands have nothing to do: she lies still, a hand to her forehead, eyes on the back of his head. 'J. Stay for breakfast.' comes at the pitch of 'That's a drink', not pleading. Then she rolls him over, turns his face on the pillow, switches off the speaker and pulls the fitted corner, all with the care she gave his collar. SC17: she lifts the pill organizer with the same face and hands as the padlock check (V01-B10), wipes under it and sets it back square. There is no wince and no pause on the full compartments or the fill slip, so the meds are seen and never played as the reason. The missed drops get one beat of stillness, then she kneels and scrubs. SC18 is the first time her thumb presses.

Constraints: both sleeves stop above the wrist bone and nothing covers the backs of her hands, so the right-hand scar, the right-thumb nick and the left-index burn stay clear. No ring on the right thumb or the left index finger. While she walks (V01-B10), the right back pocket shows a compact pistol grip above the pocket line without dragging the waistband. The V01 neckline holds one open arm of the sunglasses (V01-B08 to SC18). The bar jacket's pocket takes the tin and a straw with no bulge and can be reached from inside the jacket (SC08-SC09). The SC12 T-shirt covers to mid-thigh and carries no logo (A10). No nudity in any piece. In the open car her hair holds one way for all of V01 (loose or tied, the stylist's call) and never falls over the hand shots.

characters.role_in_story: Principal. St. Jean, called J: a serial dater three nights into drinking over a breakup. His ex's domestic-violence report ended with no charges filed (A02; the case is fictional). Bar objective: win the game and take her home. Apartment objective: get her to the bedroom. Want: to stay the wronged man in her eyes and win the night. Obstacle: every lie costs him a straw, and she already knows the answers. Change: from alive to dead, and from trying to frame the two of them himself (SC08) to being framed with her once he can no longer look (SC18). In V01 his job is to be carried: dead weight, with the one face shot at 42 s. Age 34-42, target 38. Lines and a thickening waist show the charm is older than the looks it was built on. This breaks the category default (a sculpted late-20s leading man) and the generator's drift toward young and symmetrical, so his 'hit list' swagger reads as habit. Heritage: Haitian-American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. The reason is the name St. Jean and the family D01 can give him. He is Black like VENUS so the killing doesn't read as a cross-racial story the pilot isn't telling. Lucas confirms this with S01 and V02 in view (see blockers).
characters.screen_presence: In one frame (V01): a big man in black in the passenger seat, cheek on the headrest, head turned to the door and away from her camera, so only his left jaw, ear, neck and collar show. Nothing moves but his hair, and he could be asleep. After her fingers turn his head (V01-B07), his face stays turned toward the driver's seat, where she set it, through the motel and at the table. Alive, in SC04 he sits with his shoulders rounded over the glass, elbow planted, packed duffel under the stool: a man drinking to be left alone. When she speaks he props himself up, turns his stool to her, pulls the candle over and keeps his eyes on hers. His hands join her game: a straw stood upright in the wax for himself, his phone held out to fit them both, a reach for the chimney as a trophy. In the rideshare his hands go inside her jacket for the pocket. From the lobby on, his eyes go to price and surfaces (the marble, the white room) before they go to her. He checks his teeth before he deals with the blood. At the threshold he stops half a step at the drops, then steps over them.
characters.performance_style: Three registers. At the bar (SC04-SC09) he is naturalistic and really lifted: slack and heavy in SC04, then up from her first line. He laughs at her lines, never at his own, and keeps his eyes on hers across the candle. Pushing the tab slip back unsigned is the last time he looks at it. He plays the flirt for real, so the audience wants the house to stand (Lucas: 'Jean spirits began to uplift'). The SC06 lie ('She left. Packed while I was at work. I never once raised my voice.') comes out easy, with no tell, because he believes it. SC09 is appetite, clothes on, laughing into her. From the lobby (SC10-SC14) the habit shows. His eyes reach the room before they reach her, and his lines fall into a rehearsed cadence ('Who said Rome was built in a day?', 'I ain't won a ring yet'). It peaks in the SC13 speech: a man stretching for depth and missing, who covers the stumble with 'That's for you to find out.' Sync dialogue throughout. SC15 is breathing only, recorded wild, face down with no lip-sync: slow and loud, one long stop, then a rasp. Dead (V01, SC16-SC18, S01): absolute stillness. No blink, no swallow, no breath in the chest. His eyes are open the same amount in every shot, upper lid at the top edge of the iris, aimed past the lens and never into it. Body rule (the treatment's performance rule, which the script logs as stylization, not physiology): his head moves only when her hand moves it, stays where she leaves it, and never lolls or bobs, whether the car is moving or he is at rest. SC16: his arm is loose and slides off her waist. She rolls him onto his back and turns his face toward her on the pillow, and it stays there. SC17: his arms still bend as she dresses him. V01-B01 to B06: his head holds, turned to the door, through every jolt and jump cut. V01-B07: her two fingers turn his head alone on the neck, about 60°, from the door toward the driver's seat. His torso and shoulders stay square in the seat, the collar moves only where the jaw drags it, and the head stops where she leaves it. SC18: her fingers lift toward his chin and stop, so the head stays turned to his left and his eyes miss her lens. If the director restores a push there, the push does not move it. Silent in V01 and V02.
characters.wardrobe_fit_notes: 184 cm: 7 cm taller than VENUS, 4 cm taller than DRIVER, 14 cm taller than BARTENDER. Broad shoulders well wider than the hips, thick neck, waist thickening over the belt. He must plausibly lift and carry VENUS in SC14 and read as real weight when she rolls and dresses him (SC16-SC17). Right-handed: he stands the straw and holds the phone out with his right hand (SC07-SC08). US men's L, 36 waist. Constraints: one black outfit carries SC04-SC18, because she dresses him again in SC17. The black reads as one mass against white rooms and gold light, yet lets dust glint at the collar (V01-B05). With his cheek on the headrest, the collar stands clear of the jaw, and nothing covers the side of the neck facing the driver, so collar, jaw and mole read as separate shapes from 0 to 42 s. The neckline is loose enough that a 60° head turn on a square torso drags the collar only at the jaw line and never pulls the shoulders (V01-B07). Nothing rides up or gapes on dead weight. His face takes sunglasses, with the arm on the driver's side visible. His seated head clears a small 1950s two-seater's windshield (A11; production design confirms).
visual_identity_anchors: [macro] Build: 184 cm, broad shoulders well wider than the hips, thick neck, waist thickening over the belt.

[macro] Natural hair black #17110E: tight 4A curls, dense; squared hairline, with the temple on the side facing the driver (his left) receding further. Top at 12-15 cm stretched length, picked out at the crown so it moves as one mass in the wind; sides tapered short; close beard with a hard cheek line (joint lock, stylist).

[micro] Short, wide face, wide square jaw, heavy low brows that almost meet; irises dark brown #2A1A12, unchanged in death. Dead eyes (V01-B07, B08, V02-B04 to B06, SC16-SC18): upper lid at the top edge of the iris in every shot; cornea dry and dulled with a faint grey film and no wet shine; dust on the lashes from the drive on. 'Pale, lost' lives in these details, never in a lighter iris (joint lock, makeup/VFX).

[micro] Skin #6E4631 at the cheekbone: visible pores on the nose and cheeks, two faint forehead lines, crow's feet. Dead state (V01, SC16-SC18, S01): the same hex desaturated, grey-ash at the lips, lids and under the eyes, dust in the creases after the drive. Never lightened by makeup, the grade or the 35mm look (joint lock, makeup).

[micro] A dark, lentil-sized mole on the left side of the neck (the side facing the driver), below the ear and above the collar. It is the one mark visible in the turned-head frames (0-42 s), and no other character has it.

characters.role_in_story: Supporting, one line. Works the dive bar's Thursday late shift. Objective: close JEAN's tab and clear the counter before last call. What only he does: his tab slip sends VENUS in (SC04), and the order goes through him. Age 46-54, target 50: well past 30 for the alcohol rule, and twelve years older than JEAN. Both onlookers are men because the script calls each 'him' or 'he'. Heritage: Mexican-American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. It is a casting choice, not a story need: the two onlookers are cast apart from each other and from the leads, so no heritage is tied to one job.
characters.screen_presence: In one frame: a thick-set man of about fifty behind the bar, forearms on the counter, eyes on the tab. He wants to close up. He sets the slip face-down in front of JEAN without looking at it or at him, pours without watching, and reaches for glasses the moment they are empty. Nothing he puts down lands straight. He looks at the couple only when an order is due.
characters.performance_style: Understated, deadpan. At rest his eyes are on the tab, the glasses and the till. He has one sync line ('What can I get you guys?'), said half to the counter, and no reaction to the flirt. When JEAN slides the slip back unsigned, he takes it without a look. At last call he clears the glasses without a word. In SC04 and the SC08 window shots he is background only.
characters.wardrobe_fit_notes: 170 cm: 14 cm shorter than JEAN, 10 cm shorter than DRIVER, 7 cm shorter than VENUS. Barrel chest, shoulders and hips the same width, heavy forearms. Right-handed. US men's XL. Constraints: forearms bare to the elbow, so the hand that sets down the slip reads. No logo on him or behind him (A10).
visual_identity_anchors: [macro] Build: 170 cm, barrel chest, shoulders and hips the same width, heavy bare forearms.
[macro] Shaved head with grey stubble #8E8882 at the sides and back; full grey-black moustache (joint lock, stylist). The only shaved head in the cast.
[micro] Round face, wide jaw softening under the chin, heavy greying brows with a pale scar splitting the outer end of the left brow; eyes dark brown #3A2618.
[micro] Skin #B07B55: deep forehead lines, crow's feet, broken capillaries across the nose.

characters.role_in_story: Featured, silent. A rideshare driver on a night shift, unbranded (A10), on a ride JEAN booked. Objective: keep his back seat clean; the dome light is his only move. What only he does: he watches them without being part of her game, and his dash cam is the one camera in the pilot she keeps her face out of. Age 58-64, target 61 (under 70, so no flag). His silver crown makes him the oldest face, and it reads at dash-cam resolution. Heritage: white American, recorded here and never put in a prompt. It is a casting choice, for the same reason as BARTENDER's.
characters.screen_presence: In one frame, from the cabin-facing dash cam: a thin, grey-haired man sitting upright at the edge of the frame, both hands on the wheel, his outline against the side window as streetlight slides past, with VENUS in the seat directly behind him. His right hand rises to the dome switch and flicks it on with one finger; he doesn't turn his head. His eyes go to the mirror. When VENUS switches the light off he leaves it off, and his eyes keep lifting to the mirror.
characters.performance_style: Understated, silent. He judges with his eyes only: they lift to the mirror, hold for about two seconds, then go back to the road. No reaction face and no words. The dash-cam frame is his whole performance space.
characters.wardrobe_fit_notes: About 180 cm; he reads long in the seat, head a hand's width below the roof lining. He is 4 cm shorter than JEAN and 3 cm taller than VENUS, but never stands beside either. Narrow, sloping shoulders; thin arms. Right-handed: his right hand goes to the dome switch. US men's M. Constraints: his head and shoulders must read as a clear silhouette against the side window and the passing streetlight at dash-cam resolution. His right sleeve stays clear of the wrist, so the hand reads when it rises into the dome light. Nothing branded on him or the car (A10).
visual_identity_anchors: [macro] Seated high and thin: about 180 cm, narrow sloping shoulders, long neck, a profile that reads against the side window.
[macro] Thinning silver hair #CFC9C0 cropped close, receding high, the crown bright under the dome light; clean-shaven (joint lock, stylist). The only silver hair in the cast.
[macro] Right hand shape: long, bony fingers and a narrow wrist, the outline that rises into the dome light to the switch.
[micro] Backs of the hands: raised veins, swollen knuckles, brown age spots on pale skin.
[micro] Long, narrow face, narrow jaw, heavy grey brows; skin #DDBBA3 with red weathering across the cheeks and nose, and a brown age spot at the left temple.

assumptions: JEAN's body rule (changed this round, per all three review notes). The rigor one-block rule is struck ('neck fixed', 'head and shoulders move only together, as one block', 'her two fingers turn the block'), and rigor no longer appears anywhere in the bible as a cause. The bible now carries the treatment's rule: his head moves only when her hand moves it, stays where she leaves it, and never lolls or bobs. In V01-B07 the head turns alone on the neck, about 60°, with the torso square and the collar moving only where the jaw drags it. The script logs the dusk turn as deliberate stylization, not physiology, so casting plays no medical detail. The loose arm in SC16 and the arms that still bend in SC17 are kept as performance notes. The exact angles (about compass 30° after the B07 turn, and the SC18 gaze set of about 210°, both cited in the review notes) belong to the camera plan. Casting quotes them and doesn't re-derive them.

SC18 staging. Two review notes ask for 'in SC18 her push does not move it', but the current script has no push: her two fingers lift toward his chin, then stop, and she takes the photo anyway. The bible follows the script. The rule holds either way: if the director restores a push, it does not move the head.

VENUS's hand set is locked by the film director's ruling: the 2 cm scar and the 6 mm thumb nick on the right hand, and the 1 cm burn on the back of the left index finger, all pale #C99D80. The burn carries her identity in V01-SH02 and V02-SH01, the first time any part of her is on screen (taste note: hands before faces). The 'proposal' wording is removed.

Hand-shot mapping, taken from the camera-plan citations in the review notes (the camera plan itself is not in this prompt). Right-thumb nick, on the flip icon: V01-B04 (SH07), V01-B08 (SH17), V02-B06 and SC18. Right-hand scar: V01-B07, the glasses lift and two-finger head turn (SH14-SH15); V02-B03; V01-B08, the sunglasses hook (SH16); SC18, on the phone. Left-index burn: V01-B02, the collar brush (SH02), and V02-B01 (SH01). The S03 fingertip and SC04's glovebox hand are the director's pick, and the locked marks show on whichever hand appears.

Car side. The script now writes left-hand-drive geometry: the driver's seat sits on JEAN's left, and in SC18 'at the table, that is his left'. JEAN's mole and his further-receding temple are therefore locked on his left, the side facing the driver, and VENUS's one-frame read holds: left hand on the wheel, right hand holding the phone toward him. What remains is render drift (see blockers).

The meds moved upstream. They now appear only in SC17's clean-up (the organizer full, the fill slip dated, the vial's label to the wall). In SC15 she washes her hands without meeting the mirror and the cabinet stays shut. The flat, padlock-check register is carried from the old SC15 note to SC17.

SC16 and SC17 changed upstream, and the performance notes follow them. In SC16 she waits, then rolls him and turns his face on the pillow; this is where the head rule starts in story order. SC17 adds the drops she missed: one beat of stillness, then she scrubs. In SC15 her hand passes the phone without resting on it. That is the one time her rest-and-slide gesture is skipped, and it marks the choice with no face played.

Setting. The script's decisions place the story in the US Southwest ('NO CHARGES FILED' wording) and set US vocabulary and spelling for every department, so the bible now uses both (windshield, organizer, color). The '-American' heritages, the US sizes and the assumed alcohol minimum of 25 rest on that setting. If Lucas relocates the story, the heritages are restated for the new country with no change to any anchor.

JEAN's alive register is split at the lobby. In SC05-SC09 he is really lifted, so the flirt plays for real and the season question keeps its doubt. The habit tells start in SC10 and peak in the SC13 speech, which Lucas marks as a BS answer. The SC06 lie stays tell-free.

JEAN's hair is settled (joint lock, stylist): tight 4A texture, dense, with the top at 12-15 cm stretched length, picked out at the crown so it moves as one mass. The A16 test confirms it, and the texture never changes after Lucas approves heritage.

35mm look (Lucas's relayed request, applied by the script). The casting consequences are three. Skin hex values are set under neutral light before the grade. The grade and grain never lift JEAN's skin to signal death. The micro anchors are sized to read in close-ups through grain and phone compression, and wide shots rely on the macro anchors.

The cast is exactly the script's four IDs: VENUS, JEAN, BARTENDER and DRIVER. The next man in the courthouse-steps prints (SC18, ENGINE) appears in photos only and is not cast. Production design supplies a fictional man who shares neither JEAN's build nor his hair and resembles no real person. JEAN's ex (name blacked out) is never on screen. There is no voiceover character.
Alcohol rule. No market code was given, so the minimum is assumed to be 25 and every visible face reads 30+. Targets are 34, 38, 50 and 61, and the bar background patrons in SC04-SC08 also read 30+.

Heritage. All four are casting choices, not script requirements, and none goes into an anchor or a prompt. JEAN's reason is his name. VENUS is matched to him so the killing doesn't read as a cross-racial story. BARTENDER and DRIVER are cast apart from each other and from the leads. A proposal for D01: the men she sentences vary in heritage across the season, so 'the man the system lost' is never tied to one heritage.

Lucas's 'tall slim model straight off your latest Vogue cover' is kept as height, slimness and bearing, not a glossy finish, because the tone rejects the glossy femme fatale. His optional blonde highlights are kept as a joint lock with the stylist.
'Pale' on JEAN comes only from desaturation, grey-ash at the lips and lids, dust, a dry grey-filmed cornea and eyes that never blink. It never comes from a lighter skin or iris hex.
Squaring objects belongs to VENUS alone, as the clean-horror tell. BARTENDER puts things down off-angle, and JEAN turns his stool to her rather than squaring up.

No reference was inspected; I worked only from the brief's descriptions. To stay clear of them, JEAN has no locs and no arm tattoo (ref 06), VENUS is not pale or auburn (ref 04), and no one is modeled on any face in refs 01-11.
The script has no child. No one is flagged for visible difference, religious dress, pregnancy or age 70+ (DRIVER's target is 61). Mental health is flagged for human review in the blockers.

Taste notes. 'Hands before faces': VENUS's locked hand marks carry her before her face appears at 34 s, and JEAN's neck mole holds him before his face at 42 s. 'Restraint over explanation': no knowing look to the lens, no menace register, the organizer played flat, and no physiology played on the dead body. 'Dry over sentimental': her verdicts and 'J. Stay for breakfast.' land at one dry pitch. Casting breaks no note on purpose; S01's face was already accepted upstream.
