blockers.issue: VENUS's hand set is ruled (right-hand 2 cm scar and 6 mm thumb nick, left-index 1 cm burn), but K03-HND-VENUS and the hand-double brief still carry the old set: a left-thumb nick and no burn. The shot mapping comes from the review notes' citations, not from the camera plan itself.
blockers.resolution: The generation lead re-locks K03-HND-VENUS on the ruled set, all pale #C99D80, before the stage day and before any hand shot renders (V01-B02, B04, B07, B08; V02-B01, B03, B06; SC18). The producer briefs the hand double on the same set. The generation lead checks the mapping against the camera plan. Any render showing a left-thumb nick or a missing left-index burn is discarded.

blockers.issue: Documents written to the old one-block rule may still carry it: the camera plan's V01-SH15 action and assumption (b), and any K03 or A16 test prompt that says 'fixed neck' or has head and shoulders turning together.
blockers.responsible_agent: Cinematographer, with the generation lead and the film director
blockers.resolution: Restate each one to the bible's rule: the head turns alone on the neck, about 60°, with the torso and shoulders square and the collar moving only where the jaw drags it. The head stays where her hand leaves it and never lolls or bobs. The film director confirms the SC18 staging (the script's fingers stopping short, or a push that doesn't move the head).

blockers.issue: The script's geometry is left-hand drive, but generators often mirror a vintage two-seater to right-hand drive. That would put JEAN on her left and his left-side mole out of her phone's view from 0 to 42 s.
blockers.responsible_agent: Production design, with the generation lead
blockers.resolution: Lock the car reference in K03 as left-hand drive and discard any mirrored render. If right-hand drive is ever chosen on purpose, apply the mirror rule before locking. JEAN's mole, his further-receding temple and the visible sunglasses arm move to his right, VENUS's hand marks stay, and the camera department re-checks S01's over-the-right-shoulder composition.

blockers.issue: Rights and consents have no owner yet. Source: this casting bible. Scope: (a) VENUS's laugh, the only voice in V01, V02 and D01; (b) the hand double for the hand shots in blocker 1; (c) if D01 is shot live action (A09 if_wrong), an intimacy coordinator and every performer's written consent for the SC07 insert, SC09 and SC14-SC16. Status: pending. Nothing is cleared, no performer is attached, and no one's availability, likeness or voice is claimed.
blockers.resolution: Generate the laugh, or record it from a consenting fictional-cast performer; no voice is cloned from a real person. Engage the hand double on a written release covering V01, V02 and SC18. Book the intimacy coordinator before any live-action D01 schedule. Record each clearance before the pitch pieces circulate.

blockers.issue: Generated faces can land on a recognisable real person, and S01 and V02 travel without D01's context.
blockers.resolution: Before S01 or V02 leaves the team, run a real-person resemblance check on the locked VENUS and JEAN faces, and on BARTENDER and DRIVER before any D01 material circulates. If a face reads as a real person, regenerate it within the same anchors and check again. Record the result with the producer. Status: pending.

blockers.issue: No market alcohol code was given, and the bar, the drinks and the tin put every visible adult under the alcohol rule.
blockers.resolution: Confirm the target markets. Until then the cast assumes a minimum of 25, and every visible face, bar background included, reads 30+. If any market sets a higher minimum or bans showing people drinking, re-age the cast or recut the bar scenes and S03.

blockers.issue: The script pairs a killer with medication she hasn't taken in weeks, and Lucas framed it as mental health. That is the representation risk the must-avoid list names (meds treated as the explanation for the killings), and the craft brief flags disability, which can include mental illness, for human review. The meds now appear in SC17 only.
blockers.resolution: Get a human or sensitivity review of SC17's organizer beat and of how D01 frames her meds before the pitch pieces circulate. Casting holds the beat to the padlock-check register (no wince, no pause on the compartments or the slip) and never ties her performance to a diagnosis. The reviewer confirms this or asks for changes.

blockers.issue: Heritage for all four characters is a casting choice, not a script requirement. The pieces that circulate raise the stakes: S01 and V02 make a dead Black man the key image beside a laughing woman, and they travel without D01's context.
blockers.resolution: Lucas approves or reassigns the heritages with S01 and V02 roughs in front of him, not from this text alone. If anything changes, redo skin hex, hair texture and JEAN's dead-state notes together, keep VENUS and JEAN matched or say why not, and restate the heritages if the setting moves from the US Southwest.

blockers.issue: JEAN's dead anchors depend on the A16 test. In a moving convertible, under the 35mm look, a still, open-eyed passenger must hold his identity, his dead eyes (upper lid at the top edge of the iris, a dry grey-filmed cornea, dusted lashes), a head that holds where she set it with no loll or bob, and hair that moves, because V01-B07 and V02-B04 prove death with 'the wind moves his hair'.
blockers.responsible_agent: Director / generation lead, with the stylist
blockers.resolution: Run the 5 s A16 test on the locked anchors with the 35mm look applied. It passes if the top of his hair shifts as one mass and the crown ends flutter within the 5 s, while his head holds its set angle, his torso stays square and his eyes don't blink. If the top moves too little, the stylist picks it out further within 12-15 cm and never changes the 4A texture. If the pallor or the dry cornea doesn't read through the grain, carry his death through dust, unblinking eyes and a desaturated grade, never a lighter hex, and use the parked-car fallback.

evidence.specificity: Every principal comes with measurements the stylist, director and cinematographer can use without a follow-up call: "177 cm: 7 cm shorter than JEAN, 3 cm shorter than DRIVER, 7 cm taller than BARTENDER"; "Right hand: a 2 cm scar across the back between the thumb and index knuckles, and a 6 mm nick across the back of the thumb at its first joint"; "upper lid at the top edge of the iris in every shot". Behaviour is cast rather than described with adjectives: "She handles things slowly, and whatever she puts down lands square: cans, his shoes on the white mat, the two glasses, his folded clothes, the pink cloth." All the height arithmetic checks out (184/180/177/170). One point off because JEAN's "Three registers" names only the first one ("naturalistic and really lifted"). The lobby phase and the dead phase are described but never given a register name.
evidence.distinctiveness: Nothing here could be moved into another project. "Beside the dead JEAN she blinks normally, so in a shared frame her blink is the one difference between them." "Squaring objects belongs to VENUS alone, as the clean-horror tell. BARTENDER puts things down off-angle." The repeated rest-and-slide gesture ("Her right thumb does it on the flip icon, and her fingertip does it on the chimney straw (SC07) and on the tin's lid") is skipped once, at the moment of choice: "her hand passes the phone without resting on it". JEAN's identifier is built for the turned-head frames: "A dark, lentil-sized mole on the left side of the neck (the side facing the driver)... the one mark visible in the turned-head frames (0-42 s)."
evidence.fit: The bible serves route R2's central idea directly: "Lens rule: her eyes never go into any lens, including the under-a-second flips in the V01-B04 and B08 fallbacks, where they stay on him. The first time is SC18, into her own front camera." The meds must-avoid is held in performance: "There is no wince and no pause on the full compartments or the fill slip, so the meds are seen and never played as the reason." Lucas's description is kept and sharpened: "'tall slim model straight off your latest Vogue cover' is kept as height, slimness and bearing, not a glossy finish." The reference faces are avoided on purpose: "JEAN has no locs and no arm tattoo (ref 06), VENUS is not pale or auburn (ref 04)." The alcohol rule is assumed and flagged, and nudity is excluded. Every heritage is recorded as a choice for Lucas to approve, never stated as fact.
evidence.craft: The core technique is right. Spans are within 10 years with age markers ("fine laugh lines at the outer eyes" at 34, "wide jaw softening under the chin" at 50). Each character has one asymmetry, skin hex plus texture, build given as shoulders against hips, a unique anchor, and joint locks tagged. Heritage stays out of the anchors. The rights blocker names its source, scope and owner: "Status: pending. Nothing is cleared, no performer is attached, and no one's availability, likeness or voice is claimed." It stays at 8 and not 9 for four reasons. First, DRIVER's "[macro] Right hand shape" cannot read in the widest dash-cam frame. Second, JEAN's permanent face anchor carries a makeup and VFX state ("cornea dry and dulled with a faint grey film and no wet shine"), which contradicts the bible's own "no physiology played on the dead body". Third, the consent blocker covers an intimacy coordinator but no stunt or movement coordinator for the SC14 lift or the SC16-SC17 dead-weight handling. Fourth, JEAN's second and third registers are not named.

notes.note: Retag "[macro] Right hand shape" as micro, because a hand outline doesn't hold in the widest dash-cam frame. Keep the seated silhouette and the silver crown as his two macro anchors. Add shoulders against hips to his build line ("narrow sloping shoulders... hips wider" or "level"), matching the other three.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Tag each macro (reads in the widest shot) or micro (close-up)'; 'name... build as height plus shoulders against hips'.

notes.target: Blockers · item 8 (heritage approval)
notes.note: Give Lucas a real choice instead of approve-or-reassign. Add the one alternative pairing casting would propose, with the anchor changes it forces (skin hex, hair texture, JEAN's dead-state notes), so he compares S01 and V02 roughs for two casts. Also soften the inference from the name: 'St. Jean' reads Haitian or Québécois, so present Haitian-American as a proposal tied to a D01 family detail, not as something the name settles.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Age, gender, heritage or build is story-required only if changing it forces a rewrite; otherwise it is a choice with a reason'. Quality bar: questions about direction go to Lucas.

keep: VENUS lens rule: her eyes never go into any lens, including the fallback flips, until SC18's front camera
The blink difference: she blinks less than JEAN at the bar and normally beside the dead JEAN
The rest-and-slide digit gesture (flip icon, chimney straw, tin lid), skipped once in SC15 and pressed for the first time in SC18
VENUS places everything square; BARTENDER puts things down off-angle
VENUS's locked hand marks mapped to beats, with the left-index burn as the first part of her on screen (hands before faces)
JEAN's neck mole on the driver-facing side as his identifier from 0 to 42 s, with the car-geometry blocker
The head rule: his head moves only when her hand moves it, stays where she leaves it, never lolls or bobs
'Pale' comes only from desaturation and stillness, never from a lighter skin or iris hex
JEAN's SC06 lie played with no tell; the habit tells start in the lobby and peak in the SC13 speech
'J. Stay for breakfast.' at the pitch of 'That's a drink'
Relative height arithmetic across all four characters, age spans of 10 years or less with age markers, and one asymmetry per face
The meds beat played in the padlock-check register, flagged for sensitivity review
Rights blockers (laugh voice, hand double, intimacy coordinator, real-person resemblance check, alcohol code), each with an owner and left pending
Explicit avoidance of the reference faces (no locs or arm tattoo on JEAN; VENUS not pale or auburn)

locations.description: Venus's car: a vintage open two-seater roadster with a 1950s shape (A11), drawn to match no real make. Long hood, rounded fenders, low cut-down doors, a plain oval grille with 6 horizontal bars, round lamps, no hood ornament, emblem holes filled, plain body-color hubcaps. US, 2026 ASSUMED. Left-hand drive (director's ruling): Venus drives on the left and Jean rides on the right. Rear license plate only, blank. No rearview mirror on the windshield header or the dash. Scenes: SC04, top up, parked across from the bar at night, clean. SC17 insert, in LOC-11: top down, clean, passenger seat empty. SC01-SC02 (V01-B01 to B11, V02, S01): top down, dusted. She has owned it for years ASSUMED. Before V01-B01 she dressed Jean in PR-56 and put PR-04 on him (SC17; both listed in LOC-05), seated him and loaded PR-05 into the trunk beside PR-06 and PR-07 (off screen). Wear: the black steering-wheel rim is rubbed from #2E2A26 gloss to #5A4636 matte in two 8 cm arcs at 10 and 2 o'clock, where her hands go. The driver's seat's outer bolster is darkened to #B9A98C over 20 x 8 cm from getting in and out. One real detail: the wiped arc in the dash dust where the wrist of her filming hand rests (PR-57). Background: only the road and the scrub move; there are no other cars.
locations.spatial_layout: Car 4.00 L x 1.55 W; front bumper 1.80 m ahead of the windshield base ASSUMED. Section heights above the ground, locked for the car's reference model (A09): floor pan 20 cm; seat cushion tops 35 cm, each seat 45 cm wide, backs reclined about 20° ASSUMED, back tops 90 cm; bone headrest pads 18 cm tall, tops at 108 cm; door tops 72 cm; dash top 88 cm; windshield glass 30 cm from the dash top to the header at 118 cm; steering wheel 40 cm across, center 78 cm up. Seated eye lines: Venus 110 cm, upright at the wheel, crown about 121 cm; Jean 103 cm, slumped. Top down: the header at 118 cm is the highest point, and the folded top lies in its well behind the seat backs at x 110-140, stack top 98 cm. Top up (SC04): outside height 1.30 m, bow underside 1.27 m. Walls in plan, clockwise: A driver door (west when heading north), B dash and windshield, C passenger door, D seat backs and trunk. Anchor A/B is the driver's end of the windshield base; x runs along A toward D (rearward) and y toward C, in cm. Car-frame bearing: 0° = toward C, clockwise (90° D, 180° A, 270° B = straight ahead); heading north, compass = car-frame + 90°. Cabin 115 (x) x 125 (y): dash face at x 30, wheel center at x 55, y 32, seat backs at x 105. Driver's cushion centered at y 32, passenger's at y 93. Ignition on the dash face at y 50, 74 cm up. Glovebox on the passenger dash face at y 76-106: a 30 x 14 cm lid hinged at the bottom, 70-84 cm up, with a keyhole in its knob (PR-61 key 2); she reaches it across Jean's knees in V01-B09. Trunk at x 150-215, lid hinged at its front edge, locked with key 2 (PR-61); in V01-B11 it holds exactly PR-05, PR-06 and the two PR-07 sacks. Jean's pose P1, V01-B01 to B06: cheek on the passenger headrest pad at x 108, y 100, face at car-frame 0° (toward his door, compass 90°). Pose P2, from V01-B07 (not before B07): a head-only turn set by her two fingers to car-frame 240° (compass about 330° heading north), 30° left of straight ahead, toward the driver's seat; the torso stays square to the seat in both P1 and P2. Check: from his head (x 108, y 100) the line to the phone over the PR-57 wrist arc (x 20-30, y 45-65) runs 238° to the arc's near corner and 241° to its center, so in B08 his open eyes sit frontal in her phone. P2 holds unchanged through B08, B09 and B11. At the SC18 table, seated facing south, the same set is 30° to his own left: gaze bearing about 150°. SC04: top up, passenger side curtain fitted, driver's curtain off while she films; she snaps it into place before she gets out. Parked at the far curb with the driver's side to the bar, 14 m away. SC01: the car heads north on every filmed pass, so the low west sun sits behind Venus (wall A).

props.description: Venus's phone, the hero prop. 15.0 x 7.2 x 0.8 cm ASSUMED. Matte black glass back #1A1A1A, black frame, one rear lens with a small LED video light beside it, and a front camera. One plain flush side button, 12 x 3 mm, on the left frame edge as seen from the screen, 4 cm from the top. In her upright right-hand grip her index finger lies on the button and her thumb on the right edge, within reach of the flip icon. The button press is never framed. No case, logo or text. A 6 mm oily smear on the rear lens stays in every state. The bare glass tells it apart from PR-35 (case, cracked screen). Also in LOC-05 to LOC-08 (in her jacket), LOC-10, LOC-03 and LOC-04.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: upright in her right hand at the open driver's side, zoomed on Jean through the bar window. S2 end of SC04 to SC10: screen-in in the right chest pocket of VENUS_L01's bone jacket, not recording. S3 SC11 (set off screen) to the end of SC17: face down on PR-53 at x 98, y 385, long axis along y; in SC15 her hand passes over it to reach PR-54; it leaves with her. S4 V01-B01 to B05: upright in her right hand at arm's length, wrist resting on the dash-top center (the PR-57 arc), lens on Jean's collar, recording from REC 00:00:04. In B02 the wrist lifts while her left hand crosses to his collar. The video light is off until B05 and on from B05. S5 V01-B06 (after the first 0.8 s) to B07: face up in her lap, still recording, light on. S6 V01-B08, from 52 s: upright in her right hand, REC 01:04:55, light on; her thumb goes to the flip icon and back. S7 from V01-B09 into SC18 (set off screen between B08 and B09): recording stopped, light off, in her right front jeans pocket, a flat 7 cm outline showing through the denim. S8 SC18, not before SC18: taken out and held at arm's length in her right hand in front of both of them; the first press of the flip icon turns the front camera on, and she takes the photo.

props.description: Pistol: a compact semi-automatic, 17 x 12 x 3 cm ASSUMED. Matte black polymer frame #2B2B2B, black steel slide, every marking, serial and logo ground off. It is never drawn, aimed or fired. Also in LOC-03 and LOC-04.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: grip up in her right back pocket, 6 cm showing, then shut in the glovebox beside PR-03, muzzle toward C. S2 end of SC04 to V01-B09: in the glovebox, locked with PR-61 key 2 until the off-screen unlock in LOC-11. PR-08 and PR-09 lie on top of it until they move into PR-06 there; after that it lies alone. S3 from V01-B09 through B14 and into SC18: grip up in her right back pocket, 6 cm showing; not before B09. Fallback for B09: already in the pocket, no hand on it. S4 SC18, not before SC18: dropped into PR-06 where it lies at the LOC-04 jamb (x 195-240, y 22-50, below the held frame) as she takes PR-28 out. It never goes on the table.

props.description: The metal tin: 7.0 x 5.0 x 1.8 cm, satin gunmetal #4A4D52, rounded corners, lid hinged along one long side, no embossing or text. The interior and contents are never framed. It never appears in V01 or V02. Also in LOC-05, LOC-06, LOC-08 and LOC-11 (in PR-06).
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: closed in the glovebox, hinge toward C. S2 end of SC04 to SC10: closed in the inside left pocket of VENUS_L01's jacket; PR-30 joins it in SC08, and in SC09 Jean's hand finds both inside the jacket. S3 from SC11 (set off screen) to SC12: closed on PR-42 at x 175, y 535, long axis along y, hinge side facing 90°. S4 SC12, not before SC12: slid under her fingertip to x 140, y 525; Jean turns it over and tries the lid while her fingertip stays on it, and it ends where it started. S5 SC13-SC14, not before SC13: lid raised about 100°, the open well facing 270°, toward Jean. S6 SC17, not before SC17: closed and put into the inside left pocket of the jacket on PR-62; from the end of SC17 it stays in that jacket, folded inside PR-06, through V01 and SC18.

props.description: Venus's bag: a tan waxed-canvas weekender #8C6A45, 45 x 25 x 25 cm, handles with a 60 cm drop, a darker crease worn along the handles, no logo. About 5 kg ASSUMED. Also in LOC-11 (in the trunk) and LOC-04.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04 to SC17 (ASSUMED, never framed): in the locked trunk, holding PR-28, pins already through their top edges, plus one spare pin. PR-08 and PR-09 go in from the glovebox in LOC-11 before the SC17 insert (off screen). S2 end of SC17, off screen in LOC-11: VENUS_L01's bone jacket laid on top, folded, with PR-03 in its inside left pocket; zipped. Contents unchanged through V01-B11 and into SC18. S3 V01-B11: carried in. S4 from the end of V01-B11: slumped against and half on top of PR-05 at x 195-240, y 22-50, below the held frame. S5 SC18: opened where it lies; PR-28 comes out and PR-02 goes in.

props.description: Grocery sacks: two unprinted kraft paper sacks #B8946A, 30 x 18 x 43 cm, tops rolled. Sack 1: PR-21 standing on its base with PR-25 on top, about 3 kg. Sack 2, doubled: PR-22's two full jugs upright side by side with PR-24 on top, about 8.5 kg. Also in LOC-03 and LOC-04.
props.persistent_state_notes: S0 from before SC04 (ASSUMED, never framed): in the locked trunk, so she makes no stop with Jean in the car. S1 V01-B11: upright in the trunk beside the bags, then carried in, so B11 carries exactly two bags and two sacks. S2 V01-B12: unpacked onto PR-17. S3 from the end of V01-B12: emptied and folded flat under PR-17.

props.description: Stack of long-lens prints: about 120 gloss 15 x 10 cm prints of Jean alone, going back months, held with a natural rubber band #C9A86A. The top print is Jean at the bar window. Every subject is fictional, and the storefronts and cars in the prints are blank.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: on the passenger seat cushion, band on. S2 end of SC04: swept into the glovebox on top of PR-02, then locked in (PR-61). S3 in LOC-11 before the SC17 insert (off screen, ASSUMED): moved into PR-06. The passenger seat is empty in SC17 and in all of V01.

props.description: Photocopied incident report: one US letter sheet, gray toner. A woman's name is blacked out with a #111111 marker bar, 5 x 0.6 cm. A diagonal red stamp #B22A22 reads verbatim 'NO CHARGES FILED'; these are its only legible words. No agency, seal, case number or address. Fictional (A02).
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: on the passenger seat, half under PR-08. S2 end of SC04: swept into the glovebox, folding once as it goes in, then locked in. S3 in LOC-11 before the SC17 insert (off screen, ASSUMED): moved into PR-06.

props.description: Desert dust dressing, owned by the set: fine caliche dust #C9A45C, matte, laid by hand and never blown in on camera. The collar states are agreed with the stylist and the eyes are handed to makeup. Also on PR-04's lens edges and on Jean in LOC-03 and LOC-04 (SC18).
props.persistent_state_notes: Dash D1, SC04 and SC17: none; the dash top is clean #A9ACAA satin. Dash D2 from V01-B01, not before the drive: an even film over the dash top, broken by one wiped arc at the center of its rear edge (x 20-30, y 45-65), 25 cm along the curve and 6 cm deep, wiped back to #A9ACAA where her right wrist rests. D2 holds through B11. Collar C1 V01-B01: a fine film over both shoulders and both collar points. Collar C2 V01-B02, not before B02: her hand brushes the points back to #24262B, the shoulders still dusted. Collar C3 from V01-B05, not before B03: a fresh film back on the points, glinting under the video light; it holds through B08, B11 and SC18. Eyes, a makeup hand-off from V01-B07: #C9A45C on the lashes and in the lid creases, matching the collar.

props.description: Car keys: two plain nickel-silver keys on a 25 mm steel split ring. Key 1, 5.5 cm: ignition and doors. Key 2, 4.5 cm: glovebox and trunk. No fob, tag, logo or legible cut code. Also used in LOC-11 (off screen) and in LOC-03 and LOC-04.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: key 1 in the ignition; the trunk has been locked since before SC04. As she gets out, key 2 locks the glovebox (a turn at the knob inside the scripted exit, not a new beat), and the ring goes into her left front jeans pocket. S2 in LOC-11 before the SC17 insert (off screen): key 2 unlocks the trunk and the glovebox, and both stay unlocked through V01 and SC18, so V01-B09 and B11 need no key action. S3 V01-B01 to B08: key 1 in the ignition at y 50, the ring hanging still. S4 from V01-B09 through SC18: in her left front jeans pocket, never sharing a pocket with PR-01; not before B09.

locations.product_placement: No product (R2 stretch). The device doing the job is PR-01, held in Venus's right hand at arm's length, wrist on the dash-top center, lens on Jean's collar. The phone UI is composited in finishing: an original design with no OS or maker's marks, clearance pending (A10). The upright 9:16 picture sits centered between #0A0A0A pillars. Top bar #111111, 7% of frame height: the REC dot #D7261E, 2.2% of frame width, and the timer in #F2EEE6. V01 timer, verbatim: 00:00:04, 00:06:12, 00:21:40, 00:38:15, 00:52:30, 00:53:10, 01:04:29 (B05), 01:04:37 (the first 19 frames of B06 only), 01:04:55 (B08). V02's teaser clock: 00:06:13, 00:52:30, 01:04:55, 01:04:58, 01:05:00. Bottom bar #111111, 9% of frame height, with the flip-camera icon at bottom right under her thumb: a #F2EEE6 outline of a camera body (a rounded 4:3 rectangle with a small viewfinder hump at top center) holding two curved arrows that chase each other in a circle, the generic front/rear-camera convention drawn from scratch, with no OS artwork. Size: at least 3% of V01's 16:9 frame width (58 px or more at 1920, about 9.5% of the pillar's width) and at least 6% of V02's 9:16 frame width (65 px or more at 1080). It is in the A10 clearance package. Contrast: REC dot on the bar 3.8:1; timer and icon on the bar 16.3:1; Jean's #24262B collar on the #D9CBB0 headrest 9.4:1. Clear zone: the lower-right 15% of the frame, around the icon, holds nothing but her thumb (V01-B04 and B08, V02-B06). Swap-test stand-in: the icon exists only because she won't turn the lens on herself, and its first press is SC18.

locations.description: SC01 (V01-B01 to B08, V02-B01 to B06, and the light for S01). US Southwest high desert, 2026 ASSUMED, within a day's drive of the city. A crossroads town empty for decades ASSUMED: one block of six single-story stucco storefronts, windows boarded and sign bands sanded blank. A two-lane blacktop runs north past it through scrub flats toward low hills. Right-hand traffic, a faded double-yellow center line, white edge lines. No other vehicle, person, animal or overhead wire in any shot; only the scrub moves. She passes the town twice, so the storefronts in V01-B03 at 00:21:40 are a second pass. Wear: crazed asphalt; the stop sign's face sun-chalked from red to #B8453A, letters intact, and the sign spun on its rusted post by years of wind to face the crossing instead of its approach, with nobody come to set it straight (ASSUMED, PR-10); a sand drift across the northbound lane at the crossing that no tire crosses until hers. One real detail: the stop sign nobody else will ever reach (V01-B02).
locations.spatial_layout: Exterior. x runs north along the blacktop from the town block's south end and y east from the center line, in m. Road 7.3 m wide (two 3.65 m lanes); the car keeps to the northbound lane, its passenger side at about y 2.6, Jean's head at about y 2.05. Town block on the east side (Jean's side) at x 0-45, set back 4 m from the edge line, sign bands 4.2 m high. Crossroads with an east-west graded gravel road, 6 m wide (edges x 3,097-3,103), 3.1 km north of the town: 6 min 08 s at about 30 km/h (19 mph) from the first pass at REC 00:00:04 to the stop at 00:06:12. No painted stop line (worn away). PR-10 stands on the east shoulder 2.2 m off the edge line (y 5.85), set back 9 m from the gravel edge at x 3,088, where the shoulder widens over a culvert ASSUMED. B02: she stops with her front bumper 1 m short of the gravel edge (x 3,096), PR-58 just ahead of it. Jean's head, 2.9 m behind the bumper, is then about 5.1 m north and 3.8 m west of the sign, so from the phone over the dash the sign sits about 7° right of and 11° above his head, facing the lens, with the empty crossing out of frame ahead. Loop ASSUMED, 15 min 28 s from 00:06:12 to the second pass at 00:21:40: east 2.0 km on the gravel, south 4.6 km on a gravel section road, west 2.0 km back to the blacktop 1.5 km south of the town (8.6 km at about 40 km/h, 25 mph: 12.9 min), then north 1.5 km on the blacktop at about 35 km/h, 22 mph (2.6 min). Second pass (B03, 00:21:40): north through the town again, past the crossroads (never framed), into open desert (00:38:15, about 11 km on) and toward hills 2-5 km east (00:52:30). The low sun sits in the west, behind the driver; blue dusk by B05.

props.description: US stop sign: a 75 cm red octagon, sheeting sun-chalked to #B8453A with a white border, on a weathered galvanized post #8E8C86, bottom edge 2.1 m up. Spun on its post by wind (ASSUMED) to face about 325° (north-west), square to the lens in B02 instead of to the approach. Its only legible text is 'STOP' in white, verbatim; composite it if the letters distort. No stickers or graffiti. Back: plain galvanized #8E8C86.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 V01-B02 and V02-B01: static, facing 325°, the same in every shot. Fallback if the director wants it square to the road (facing 180°): the lens then sees only its back, and the octagon reads by silhouette alone.

props.description: Storefront sign bands: six boarded storefronts with sign bands sanded to bare #C8B79A. No lettering, ghost letters, logos or numbers. Plywood window boards #8C7A5E.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 V01-B01 (first pass) and B03 (second pass): static, the same boards in the same order, blank.

props.description: Sand drift: fine sand #C9B28A, matte, 40 cm wide and 1-2 cm deep, wind-rippled across the northbound lane at x 3,096.0-3,096.4, just ahead of her stopped bumper. Continuity-only: no planned view sees the road ahead of the car (B02 looks back past Jean; B06's wide is elsewhere at dusk). Kept so any added forward view matches.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 through the stop in V01-B02: unbroken. S2 from her pull-away in B02, not before B02: two tire tracks 16 cm wide, 1.30 m apart, pressed to a darker #A89470 with 1 cm ridges along their edges. S3 after the second pass, not before B03: a second pair crossing the first.

locations.product_placement: No product. The stop sign carries the scene's one detail, and 'STOP' is the only word here. The only motion is the scrub, which stays lower in contrast than Jean's #24262B collar in the same frame.

locations.description: SC02 (V01-B09 to B11). An abandoned US Southwest roadside motel, built about 1958 and shut about 25 years ago ASSUMED (ref 08 as the brief describes it): a two-story stucco room block with a gutted upper floor, a single-story office, a long carport, a peeling sign on steel legs and dry palms. Venus has used room 3 for weeks (LOC-04). The office step's unbroken dust is her proof that nobody has come. Her own traffic has worn one bare track, 40 cm wide, #A89878 packed dust against #B7A98C loose, about 6 m from the carport bay to her door. Background: palm fronds and scrub move, and a loose sign panel ticks. The highway stays empty.
locations.spatial_layout: Site 60 x 35 m. Wall A is the highway frontage (south). x runs east and y north, in m; bearing 0° = north. The driveway enters at x 17-24. Sign PR-12 on steel legs at x 8, y 3: the MOTEL box is 6.0 x 1.8 m with its top at 9 m; the OFFICE arrow is 3.0 x 0.8 m at 5 m, pointing east. Office 6 x 6 m at x 9-15, y 12-18, its door centered on the south face at x 12, with PR-14 in front at y 11.6-12.0. Room block at x 16-59.2, y 18-27, 6.5 m high: twelve ground-floor rooms 3.6 m wide, each door at the east end of its frontage. Room 2 is x 19.6-23.2 (door x 22.1-23.0); her room, room 3, is x 23.2-26.8, door PR-15 at x 25.7-26.6, facing 180°. Carport at x 16-30, y 12-18: corrugated roof at 2.6 m on steel posts at 3.6 m centers. The car noses in facing 0° at x 21.0-22.55, y 13.5-17.5, passenger side toward her door, trunk about 6 m from it; Jean's head at about x 22.0, y 14.6. Jean in P2 (car-frame 240°, compass about 330°): his gaze crosses the driver's seat and lands on room 2's frontage at about x 20.0, 2 m west of room 2's door and about 6 m west of hers. V01-B09: engine off; PR-61 goes to her left front pocket and PR-02 to her right back pocket, and PR-01 is already in her right front pocket; her lean from the driver's seat to the glovebox crosses his gaze line about half a meter in front of his face. B10: she walks south-west about 10 m from the car to the office step and tugs the padlock from the gravel, never standing on the step. B11: she carries from the trunk north-east to her door, on the side his face is turned from; the driver's seat his gaze crosses is empty. Palms at x 3, 34 and 46, y 5. US, right-hand traffic.

props.description: Motel sign on steel legs. The box face is peeling cream enamel #E2D8C2 over gray primer #9A968C, with 'MOTEL' (verbatim) in letters 1.2 m high, faded teal #5F8A86, a third of them flaked. Below it, the red arrow #A83A2C reads 'OFFICE' (verbatim). One loose 60 x 40 cm face panel at the top right ticks in the wind. No other text.

props.description: Office padlock and hasp: a 5 cm brass padlock #8C6E3A, dulled to a green patina #6F7A5A, on a rusted steel hasp #7A4A2A, 110 cm up on a plywood-boarded office door #8C7A5E.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 V01-B10: locked. She tugs it, it knocks on the hasp and hangs back in the same position, still locked.

props.description: Her room door: swollen plywood, 90 x 203 cm, faded turquoise paint #5E8C8A over #3F5F5C. The room-number plate is gone, leaving two screw holes. By the latch edge, a 20 x 30 cm patch at 143-173 cm is rubbed to bare wood #8A6E4E by her shoulder.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 V01-B11: closed. S2 V01-B11, not before B11: shouldered open to 90°, scraping over grit.

locations.product_placement: No product. The only legible text is 'MOTEL' and 'OFFICE', verbatim. The pistol grip (#2B2B2B matte) has to read in her back pocket, so the stylist is asked for light-wash denim around #8FA3B8 (5.5:1). Pocket map from V01-B09: phone outline in the right front pocket, keys in the left front, grip in the right back. Only the grip shows.

locations.description: The motel room: SC03 (V01-B11 to B14, S02) and SC18. Room 3 of the 1958 block ASSUMED, stripped (no bed frame, no TV). Venus has used it on and off for about five weeks ASSUMED, counted by nine emptied gallon jugs. It is where she builds the wall and brings each man afterwards (A14). Walls: period knotty-pine tongue-and-groove in 15 cm vertical boards, aged to amber #7A5A3C under dull satin varnish; pins go straight in. Two-slot NEMA 1-15 outlets with brown bakelite plates, all dead; the wall-B plate at y 120, 30 cm up, is missing. Before V01-B12 she left at least two days ago ASSUMED, with the bedroll laid out, the wall up and the lantern off on the table. Wear, all inside the held frame: a chalky dust film #A08D72 over the fir floorboards, broken where her feet go at y 380-480. There, a bare track 40 cm wide, dull satin #5C4A38, runs along y 440-480 behind the chairs from the bedroll head (x 80) to the jugs (x 330), and a 50 x 40 cm scuffed patch in the same #5C4A38 lies at x 125-175, y 380-420, under the table's north edge where her feet go when she sits. Three overlapping jug rings, 16 cm across, in dull #9C8468 on the table's west end at x 122-150, y 372-398. A paler 60 x 80 cm rectangle #A88458 on wall C at x 283-343, heights 155-235, where the motel's own picture hung. About 20 empty pin holes, 1 mm with 3 mm dark halos #4A3626, at x 278-284, where she re-pinned the last column. Background: nothing moves; the wind pushes at the door. One real detail: PR-25, the printer, planted for SC18.
locations.spatial_layout: 3.6 W x 4.8 D x 2.6 H ASSUMED. Walls clockwise: A south (entrance), B west, C north, D east. Anchor A/B; x along A toward D and y toward C, in cm; bearing 0° = toward C (compass north). Wall A: window at x 40-140 (sill 95, head 200), boarded with plywood #8C7A5E, a 15 cm gap at the top showing dark sky. Door PR-15 at x 250-340, hinged at x 340, swings in toward D over x 250-340, y 0-90; it sticks at 35° until shouldered. View out: the carport and the car. PR-05 and PR-06 lie just inside the latch-side jamb at x 190-245, y 10-50, below the held frame; in SC18 she takes PR-28 out of PR-06 there and drops PR-02 in. Wall D: PR-19 S1 at x 315-360, y 280-325, facing 270°. North-east corner: the nine emptied jugs PR-23 at x 330-360, y 400-475. Wall B: bedroll PR-26 at x 10-80, y 190-400, with the wall-B section of PR-20 above it at y 205-380, heights 150-234. Wall C: the main PR-20 at x 15-277.5, heights 95-239; the bare pine at x 280-345, with the paler rectangle, stays empty until SC18. Table PR-17 (120 x 70 x 74) at x 120-240, y 330-400. Chairs PR-18 and PR-19 stand on its north side with their backs to wall C; the back tops at 88 cm sit below the photos' 95 cm bottom edge. They face 180°, seat centers at y 420, x 150 (hers) and x 210 (Jean's). Tabletop before B12: PR-16 (off) at x 180, y 365, and the rings. From B12: PR-16; PR-25 at x 145, y 340, slot facing 180°; PR-24 at x 195-225, y 340-360; PR-21 at x 182-198, y 382-397; PR-22 at x 206-238, y 382-397; PR-07 folded flat beneath. The floor enters frame only beyond about y 375, which is why the jugs and the wear sit at y 380-480.

props.persistent_state_notes: S1 V01-B12 to B14: seat center at x 150, y 420, facing 180°. S2 SC18, not before SC18: moved to x 165, its seat edge touching PR-19's, on Jean's right (west).

props.description: The photo wall: about 250 gloss 15 x 10 cm long-lens prints of Jean (ASSUMED count), every one landscape, on steel pins on a fixed 17.5 x 12 cm grid (gaps of 2.5 cm and 2 cm, each print within ±1 cm of its cell). Wall C: 15 columns x 12 rows = 180 prints at x 15-277.5, heights 95-239. Wall B: 10 columns x 7 rows = 70 prints at y 205-380, heights 150-234. He is alone in every print; none shows the two of them together (verified fact). Subjects: a bar window, an unbranded gas pump with no numerals, crossing a street. About half are night shots and half day, with Jean in black in every one. No text in any print.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 V01-B12 to B14 and S02: all 250 on the grid, the bare pine at x 280-345 empty. S2 SC18, not before SC18: PR-28, then PR-27, pinned into the bare pine.

locations.product_placement: No product. The jobs here belong to PR-20 (none of them together) and to PR-25 with PR-27, the pilot's payoff (A06). The printer sits on Venus's side because she works it; the oranges and, in SC18, the sunglasses sit in front of Jean. The lantern #F2EEE6 on the #5E4632 table gives 7.6:1. No gun on the table in SC18: PR-02 goes into PR-06 at the jamb, below the held frame. Frame lock: V01-B13 and S02 name more than five props, over the craft limit but forced by the script. Lock order: PR-20, PR-16, PR-24, PR-25, PR-19; PR-21, PR-22, PR-23 and PR-26 are held by count and position. Nothing moves in V01-B13 to B14.

locations.description: The dive bar and its street: SC04 (seen from the car), SC05 to SC08, and S03. A dive bar in an unnamed US Southwest city, 2026, open about 40 years ASSUMED, in a 1950s single-story strip of painted brick #7E4B3A with a flat stucco parapet and one fan palm in a sidewalk cutout. LED cobra-head streetlights, so the only amber on the sidewalk is the bar's window spill. Inside is a long, narrow regulars' room, after refs 01-03 as the brief describes them: amber wall sconces, a red neon strip over the back bar, a green-glowing bottle fridge, candles in glasses on the counter, and a chalkboard menu smudged past reading. Thursday, near empty: three patrons in silhouette at the far end and one bartender. It is Jean's third night on the same stool: in PR-56 with PR-04 hooked in his placket, PR-41 on the footrail and PR-05 under the stool, all first seen here through the window in SC04. Wear: the varnish worn to raw #6B4A30 over a 40 x 25 cm patch at his stool from elbows; dozens of faint dull rings #5A4030 on the counter; the brass footrail rubbed bright #C9A15A in front of each stool. Background: the patrons move slowly, stay lower in contrast than the straws, and never cross the straw house or the candle. One real detail: PR-30 standing in candle wax.
locations.spatial_layout: 6.0 W x 14.0 D x 3.2 H ASSUMED. Walls: A street front (south), B west, C back, D east. Anchor A/B; x along A toward D and y toward C, in cm. Wall A: glazed door at x 470-560, swinging in toward D; a plain front window with no lettering at x 40-440, sill 80, head 270. View out: the street and, 14 m away at the far curb, the car (LOC-01), driver's side to the bar. Wall B: back-bar shelves at y 150-1250, bartender's aisle at x 45-100, counter at x 100-160, top 107 cm, running y 200-1200. Ten stools at 90 cm centers from y 260, seats at 76 cm. Jean is on stool 2 (y 350), in the window's sightline, with PR-05 at x 175-225, y 336-364; Venus takes stool 3 (y 440). PR-31 starts at x 115, y 260; the straw caddy stands at x 130, y 480; the straw house is centered at x 130, y 395, between their glasses. Red neon at 210 cm over y 250-900; fridge at y 950-1050. Wall C: restroom door at x 400-480. Wall D: booths, sconces at 190 cm. Street: right-hand traffic, 12 m curb to curb, 3 m sidewalks, LED cobra heads (4000K ASSUMED), one fan palm at x 620. The rideshare (LOC-06) stops at the bar's curb, x 0-500, right side to the curb.

props.description: House straws and caddy: plain white paper straws, 20 cm x 6 mm, uncoated #EFE9DC, about 40 standing in a clear glass tumbler. The house lies flat on the counter: the base parallel to the counter edge at x 148, y 385-405, through PR-33's ring; side walls from x 128 to 148 at y 385 and y 405; the back wall at x 128; two roof straws rising from the back corners to an apex at x 111, y 395, pitched toward wall B so the house reads upright from the stools.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC05: one straw, the base, laid in PR-33's fresh wet ring. S2 SC06: the left wall added, making an L. S3 SC06: the left wall drawn out, back to S1 (her first verdict). S4 SC08 window montage: the full house, 6 straws, the ring dried to dull #5A4030 until PR-32 S3 re-wets it. S5 SC08 (= S03), not before PR-32 S3: her fingertip draws one roof straw out toward the counter edge, leaving 5; the base lies in the re-wet ring, its middle 8 cm damp and darker (#D9CFBC). S6 SC08 last call, not before last call: every flat straw gone.

props.description: The chimney: one PR-29 straw used upright. From SC07 on, a 1 cm cream wax ring #E8DCC0 stays on its foot. Also in LOC-06 and LOC-08.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC07: pushed 1 cm into PR-31's wax pool, standing 19 cm above the wax and leaning 5° toward Jean; her fingertip rests on its top and slides off, and it stays standing. S2 SC08 last call, not before SC08: plucked by Venus before Jean reaches it, into the inside left pocket of her jacket beside PR-03. S3 SC12: standing in the ice of her PR-43 tumbler, foot on the glass floor, leaning about 25° against the rim, top about 10 cm above it. S4 SC13-SC14, not before SC13: flat on PR-42 at x 160, y 488-508, parallel to the table's long axis, over a 20 x 1.2 cm wet mark. S5 SC17, not before SC17: dropped into PR-60 on top of the folded pink PR-46, as the script has it, and the wet mark wiped away (the review conflict is in blockers).

props.description: Bar candle: a cream pillar #E8DCC0 burned down to 6 cm, 7.5 cm across, in a 9 cm amber glass tumbler #8A4E1E, with a soft 1 cm wax pool. Lit.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC05-SC06: at x 115, y 260. S2 from SC07, not before SC07: pulled by Jean to x 112, y 418, 13 cm off the house's roof on Venus's side. S3 SC08: in the same spot, holding PR-30 until last call.

props.description: Two Naked and Famous coupes: plain stemmed clear coupes, bowls 11 cm across, feet 7 cm, 15 cm tall. A pale amber drink #D9A441, chilled, no garnish; each new round sweats down the stem. Clearance for the name is pending (A10).
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC05: set down full at x 140, y 350 (his) and x 140, y 440 (hers). S2 SC06: hers two-thirds full after the drink. S3 SC08 window montage, not before SC08 (scripted): his fresh, sweating coupe set down on the base straw over the dried ring at x 148, y 395; it rocks; he lifts it off, laughing, and sets it back at x 140, y 350; its wet foot leaves a fresh 7 cm ring. S4 SC08 (= S03): both low, one on either side of the house. S5 SC08 last call: cleared.

props.description: Jean's rocks glass: heavy clear glass, 8 cm across, whiskey dregs #8B5A2B, leaving an 8 cm wet ring.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04-SC05: at x 148, y 395. S2 SC05, not before SC05: moved to x 140, y 320, leaving its wet ring at x 148, y 395; the ring dries by the SC08 montage. S3 SC08: cleared.

props.description: Tab slip: plain thermal paper #F4F1EA, 8 x 15 cm, figures as unreadable gray marks, no bar name, on a small black tray.
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC04: set in front of Jean at x 150, y 360. S2 SC05: slid back unsigned to x 105, y 360, then taken away.

props.description: Jean's phone: 15 x 7 cm, in a scuffed matte black silicone case with its top-left corner split, a spiderweb crack across the top-right third of the screen (#D9D9D9 lines on black glass), no logo. Its screen content is never legible. Also in LOC-06 (the curb).
props.persistent_state_notes: S1 SC08: held at arm's length by Jean on its front camera. S2 SC08: in Venus's hand, photographing him alone. S3 SC08: handed back and pocketed. S4 SC09 at the curb: out in Jean's hand while Venus leans in and types the drop-off, then back in his pocket.

props.description: Jean's sunglasses: black acetate frame #111111, 14 cm wide, dark gray lenses #2A2E33, no logos. Carried in Jean's shirt placket (style bible). First seen through the bar window in SC04. Also in LOC-06 to LOC-08, LOC-10, LOC-01, LOC-03 and LOC-04.
props.persistent_state_notes: S0 SC04 to SC14: hooked by the left arm in Jean's placket over the fastened second button, held with a clear thread tack (costume rigging, never acted), lenses hanging out; seen through the bar window and at the bar, which plants them before V01. S1 SC15: unhooked by Venus, folded, lenses up, on top of his folded shirt on PR-55 (LOC-10). S2 SC17, not before SC17: taken from that pile and put on his face. S3 V01-B01 to B06: on his face, a light PR-57 film at the lens edges; only the left arm shows to the phone. S4 V01-B07: open in her right hand while two of her fingers turn his chin. S5 from V01-B08's first second through B14 and into SC18: one open arm hooked into her shirt neckline at center, lenses hanging out; not before B08. S6 SC18: folded, lenses up, on PR-17 at x 200-214, y 365-370, just north of PR-24.

No outside pocket, logo, tag or branded zip pull. About 6 kg ASSUMED. First seen under his stool in SC04. Also in LOC-06, LOC-08, LOC-01 (the trunk), LOC-03 and LOC-04.

locations.product_placement: No product. Decorum is read in straws, so the straws do the job here. White #EFE9DC on the #3A2418 counter gives 12:1, so the house reads with the sound off in S03 and through the window in SC08. In S03 nothing but her fingertip moves within 30 cm of the house, and the chimney (PR-30 S1) may stand at the frame edge. Must stay blank: every bottle label on the back bar (blank cream #D8CFBC paper), the fridge glass and its contents, the chalkboard (smudges only), the neon (a plain line), the coasters, the window, PR-04's arms and PR-05.

locations.description: SC09: the bar curb, then the rideshare's back seat, seen from a cabin-facing dash cam. A generic late-model midsize sedan, dark gray #2F3236, with no badges and no rideshare stickers, logos or trade dress (A10). The driver keeps a clean cabin: the rear seat cloth is pilled to #3A3D42 fuzz over 25 x 15 cm at both outer bolsters, and a plain black phone mount sits on the dash. Jean's duffel lies across the footwell. Background: cool LED streetlight slides across the side glass; nothing outside is legible. One real detail: the dash cam, a second recording of Jean that Venus doesn't control and keeps her face out of.

Walls: A the right (curb) side, with the right rear door at x 40-110 as the entry; B the rear shelf and back glass; C the left side, doors shut; D the windshield and dash. Anchor A/B, the right rear corner; x along A toward D (forward) and y toward C, in cm; bearing 0° = toward C, clockwise (90° D, 180° A, 270° B). Rear bench at x 20-70, y 5-145, seat 35 cm. Venus sits at y 100, directly behind the driver; Jean sits at y 40 by the door, slouched into the right rear corner. PR-01 is in her right chest pocket, and PR-03 and PR-30 in her inside left pocket, which his hand reaches inside the jacket. PR-05 lies across the footwell at x 72-100, y 45-95. Driver front left at y 95-135 (US left-hand drive). Dash cam PR-36 at the top of the windshield at x 172, y 110, on the driver's side of the rearview mirror (y 75), lens facing 270° onto the bench. From there Jean in the far corner faces it, and Venus, leaning over him, shows it the back of her head; the blocking is the director's. locations.description: Venus's building, the lobby and the stairs to her door: SC10. A renovated 1920s downtown mid-rise in the same unnamed US Southwest city, 2026 ASSUMED, where she has lived about two years ASSUMED. At night there is no doorman, and no residents are seen or heard. Honed white marble, satin brass and a quiet stair. Wear: the marble is polished to a gloss path 90 cm wide from the street door to the stair foot (#EDEAE4 gloss within #E9E6E0 honed). One real detail: the marble curtail step at the stair foot, rounded and projecting, the one she warns him about ('Mind the step'). The enclosed rear service bay behind the lobby is LOC-11.
locations.spatial_layout: Lobby 8.0 W x 6.0 D x 4.2 H, floor to floor 4.40 m ASSUMED. Walls: A street (south), B west, C north, D east. assumptions: Every hex is a pre-grade value under an even key. The 35mm look, lenses and lighting belong to the camera department. The smallest marks (3-5 mm drops, 1 mm pin holes, the 6 mm lens smear) are sized for close views. Every prop state is keyed to a script beat, not to a shot.

Place and year: an unnamed US Southwest city and desert, 2026 (ASSUMED), on the script's one continuous timeline. Locks: right-hand traffic, left-hand-drive cars, rear license plates only with every plate blank, English signage, a red octagon 'STOP', NEMA 5-15 outlets in the 2026 building, and two-slot NEMA 1-15 outlets in the 1958 motel.

US vocabulary and spelling throughout, per the script's decision, because these words go straight into generation prompts: hood, fenders, windshield, trunk, curb, tire, license plate, organizer, color, center, gray, galvanized, two-story, outlets, medicine cabinet, roller shade, step trash can, weekender, pants. A few of the script's own words are kept verbatim: 'service lift' and 'roller door' (SC17), each glossed once in LOC-11 as a freight elevator and a roll-up door, plus 'tap' and 'basin' (SC11, SC15).

Every dimension, weight, age and tenure is ASSUMED from its category, since none is verified. That covers the car section, the rooms, the tin, the printer, the prints, the bag weights, the 1958 motel, about five weeks at the motel, about two years in the apartment, and the desert loop.

The car section is locked for its reference model (A09): cushion tops 35 cm, dash top 88 cm, windshield header 118 cm with no rearview mirror, pad tops 108 cm, eye lines Venus 110 cm and Jean 103 cm. These are design values, not measurements, and any change comes back to production design.

P2 is built to option (b), and the SC18 left/right blocker is closed. P2 is car-frame 240° (compass about 330° heading north), a head-only turn with the torso square in P1 and P2. At the SC18 table, facing south, it becomes about 150°, 30° to his own left. The check for the reviewers: from Jean's head (x 108, y 100) to the phone over the PR-57 wrist arc (x 20-30, y 45-65), the offsets run dx -78 to -88 and dy -35 to -55, which is 22-35° left of straight ahead. The line runs 28.5° left (car-frame 241.5°) to the arc's center and 32° left (238°) to its near corner, with the lens a few cm above the wrist. The reviewers' 33° / 237° sits inside that spread, and 240° splits it. This replaces the package review's 300° / 210°, which turned his face 30° away from her and broke V01-B07 ('toward her'), B08's frontal eyes (A16) and SC18 ('his left').

LOC-03 is re-keyed to P2. Jean's head sits at about x 22.0, y 14.6 on the site. At compass 330° his gaze crosses the driver's seat and lands on room 2's frontage at about x 20.0, some 6 m west of her door. Her B09 lean to the glovebox crosses that line; her B10 and B11 routes do not.
Left-hand drive is the director's ruling. The casting car-side blocker is closed, so K01 and K02 can lock (a revision note moved out of LOC-01).

Jean's clothes are #24262B and his shoes #2A2624 (style bible values) in every palette and state. His collar on the bone headrest measures 9.4:1. Revision note moved out of LOC-01's product placement: the version before last gave 6.8:1 in error, and #111111 would give 11.8:1. The shoes on the mat recheck at 12.9:1, which was written as 12.8:1 before (a rounding difference).

Each prop is listed once, where it first appears in story time. PR-04, PR-05 and PR-56 move to LOC-05, since all are first seen through the bar window in SC04, and LOC-01, LOC-08 and LOC-10 cross-reference them. PR-41 was not named in the note but moves under the same rule. LOC-08 and LOC-10 each still keep more than two props of their own.

PR-04 follows the style bible. From SC04 to SC14 it hangs by its left arm from the placket on a clear thread tack. In SC15 it lies folded on his folded shirt, and from SC17 it is on his face. PR-05 has no outside pocket, and the old line banning anything from the placket has been removed from PR-56.

'Inside left pocket' is used in PR-03 S2/S6, PR-30 S2 and PR-62 S3. PR-06 carries the folded bone jacket, with PR-03 inside it, from the end of SC17 through V01-B11 and SC18. It is packed off screen in LOC-11, so the white apartment stays bare.

PR-30's end state follows the final script: in SC17 the flat straw goes into the trash on top of the pink cloth, and she pockets only the tin. It does not follow the review note that keeps the straw in the jacket, and that conflict is raised as a blocker.

LOC-04 follows the film director's framing numbers: the bags inside the latch-side jamb (x 190-245, y 10-50) below the held frame, the jugs in the north-east corner in ranks of 5 and 4, and the floor wear at y 380-480. PR-02 S4 now has her drop the gun into PR-06 at the jamb as she takes PR-28 out, below the held frame. This replaces the package review's tabletop placement, because SC18's table holds the lantern, the oranges and the printer and no gun is written there. The request for a framing check on the gun is withdrawn. If the director wants the gun seen in SC18, it goes to the writer first as an addition.
SC17's opening insert has its own location, LOC-11, because the script's SC17 heading names it (a revision note moved out of LOC-07). LOC-07 covers SC10 only.

Keys: PR-61 key 2 locks the glovebox and the trunk. That way the gun, the prints, the report and the next man's prints are never left unlocked overnight in a soft-top on a city street, which follows the script's own SC04 reasoning. Key 2 turns at the glovebox knob as she gets out in SC04, inside the scripted exit. It unlocks both off screen in LOC-11 before the insert, so V01-B09 and B11 need no key action. scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat B07 (42.0-50.0): close on her right hand turning his chin. His open eyes are the one face shot (taste note: hands before faces). She wants him to look back at her. Two things stop her: he is dead, and she won't turn the lens on herself. B01 (0-4), to wake him to the drive: she laughs loud on the mic, the way you laugh at a lover who sleeps through the best part, and the frame jolts. B02 (4-10), to make him presentable: a full stop at a sign nobody else will ever reach. Real detail: she obeys a stop on an empty road. Her left hand brushes the dust off him, flattens his collar, rests a beat and pulls away. B03 (10-18) is a hold: three jumps and the pose never changes, which is the joke. B04 (18-26), to get into the picture: her right thumb rests 2.2 s on the flip icon, played as shyness, then slides off, and she laughs. B05 (26-34), to keep seeing him as the light goes: the video light comes on. B06 (34-42) shows her face for the first time. Her head is turned about 45° to him and she laughs with her eyes on him, never on the road or any lens. No knowing look, no lip bite. B07: the dark is her excuse to take off his sunglasses. She draws them forward off his face from the near side and never reaches round him. Then she turns his face toward her own seat, and her laugh stops. Her fingers stay on his chin 1.2 s after his head stops. Play no shock, because she already knows. B08 (50-56), back behind the lens: she hooks his sunglasses at her own neckline and laughs more softly. His eyes now aim just past the lens toward her. Her thumb rests only 1.2 s: 'not like this, not yet'. JEAN, the head-alone rule, LOCKED for all of V01, S01 and D01's dead beats: his head moves only when her hand moves it. It turns alone on the neck with torso and shoulders square, stays where she leaves it, and never lolls or bobs with the car, a bump or her laugh. No blink, no breath. CONFIRMED: his right forearm lies slack along the passenger door top and never moves (SC01-SC02, S01).
scenes.blocking: LOC-01, top down, in LOC-02. The car heads north in the northbound lane, with the low west sun behind the driver's side (wall A). VENUS sits in the driver seat (y 32), left hand on the worn 10 o'clock arc. PR-01 is upright in her right hand at arm's length, wrist on the PR-57 arc (x 20-30, y 45-65). The lens aims back across Jean's left shoulder toward his door, so PR-11 and PR-10 pass behind his head. JEAN is in P1: torso square in the seat, facing north. His head is turned 90° right on the neck, right cheek on the pad (x 108, y 100), face to his door (car-frame 0°, compass 90°). PR-04 is on, with its right arm trapped between his temple and the pad. His right forearm lies slack along the door top (72 cm), the hand over the outer edge. The phone sees only his collar, left jaw, left ear, left sunglasses arm and neck mole. Wind is relative, nose to tail. B02: the front bumper stops at x 3,096 with PR-58 just ahead. PR-10 sits about 7° to the door side of his head and 11° above it, facing the lens. Line of action: the road, always north. Every full-width setup stays on or west of the car's centerline. From B06 to 45.0 the camera is ahead of the car, about 10° west of her straight-ahead line, looking back south. In B06 she reads as a deep three-quarter, laughing at him, and Jean is a lost profile: the back of his head and the left sunglasses arm. 41.6-45.0 is a medium two-shot, both of them waist up. Her right hand crosses in front of his face on the windshield side, takes PR-04's left arm at the hinge and draws the frame north along the pad toward the windshield. The right arm slides out from under his cheek, and the lift travels toward the lens. At 45.0 the camera is on the front axis, on or just west of the centerline, and the size steps in to a close shot of his head and her two fingers, his face about half the frame height. Her two fingers hook the windshield side of his chin and turn his head alone 120° on the neck, through dead ahead, to P2: car-frame 240° (compass 330°), 30° past dead ahead toward her seat. From this axis his gaze passes the lens on its west side, toward her, and he reads as a three-quarter with both eyes. P2 holds through B08 and SC02, and at the SC18 table it becomes 30° to his left. B08: PR-01 is back on the wrist arc at about y 60, a hand's width (8 cm) to the passenger side of his gaze line, so his eyes read frontal and centered, aimed about 5° past the lens toward her. 9:16: the phone frames are native upright. In B07 her hand and his face stay inside the middle third on both axes, because V02-B03 uses 42.8-43.8 and 45.0-46.0.

scenes.emotional_shift: Hers. Before (B01-B06): laughing and filming, eyes on him. Trigger (B07), seen by the camera: she turns his face toward her seat, and his open eyes land facing her side and still miss her face. After: no laugh for 8 s, and her fingers stay on his chin 1.2 s. In B08 she takes his sunglasses for herself and goes back behind the lens. The laugh returns softer and the thumb rest is shorter (1.2 s against 2.2 s), so the same gesture now reads 'not like this, not yet'. B04 is a hold: no trigger, the same state, shyness. Up to B07, the viewer's shift from lover to dead man comes from his stillness, not from any change in her.
scenes.transition_in: The pilot opens with no fade: from black straight into the phone's upright frame at REC 00:00:04. Her laugh and the wind on the mic start on frame one.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut with a time jump to last light: from B08's phone frame (thumb leaving the icon, wind on the mic) to B09's full-width carport on 35mm. The mic wind cuts dead and the cooling engine's ping starts on the cut. The eye goes from his eyes at the center of the upright frame to the car under the MOTEL sign, also at center.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' B04 and B08 carry it: twice her right thumb rests on the flip-camera icon over him, then slides back. Cut this and the viewer loses the want: a woman who films a man for an hour and can't turn the lens around. The wall, the table for two and SC18's press would then read as a collector's trophies.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Head-alone rule, LOCKED. Method: G, with one locked head plate reused wherever the pose holds. Acceptance: in B01-B06 his head holds P1 in every plate, through every laugh, jolt and bump. In B07 it moves only during the 1.8 s turn, never during the glasses lift, and turns alone on the neck with torso and shoulders unmoved; the collar shifts only where the jaw drags it. From 46.8 it holds P2 through B08 and SC02. Risk: a bob reads alive, a loll reads as a rag doll, and a shoulder turn breaks SC02 and SC18.

Glasses lift, B07 42.8-44.4. Method: G on the locked head plate; if the trapped right arm drags his head, composite PR-04 as a CG element drawn off by her hand plate. Acceptance: his head holds against the pad, and the only movement is the lenses clearing his face; the right arm slides out from under his cheek without lifting it. Risk: the head follows the glasses and reads alive, which breaks the head rule.

The 120° turn, from P1 (90° right) to P2 (30° left). Acceptance: P1 reads as a sleeping head resting on the pad, not a wrenched neck, and the turn passes dead ahead with no overshoot or bounce. Risk: an extreme P1 reads as a broken neck. Fallback: ease P1 to about 80° right, with the cheek still on the pad.

Cut at 45.0. Acceptance: both setups are ahead of the car and neither is east of the centerline. The size steps from a medium two-shot to a close shot of his head (face about half the frame height), so the cut reads as a cut in and not as a jump cut, since the axis moves only about 13°. His gaze passes the lens at least 10° on its west side. The lens choice is the DP's. Risk: an east setup puts his gaze into the lens.

Right forearm, confirmed. Acceptance: it lies slack along the passenger door top, hand over the outer edge, in every plate of B01-B11 and in S01. It never moves, including under her lean in B09, and never enters the phone frame.

Phone UI (REC dot, timer, flip icon). Method: composited in finishing; an original design, clearance pending (A10). Acceptance: the timer reads 00:00:04, 00:06:12, 00:21:40, 00:38:15, 00:52:30, 00:53:10, 01:04:29, 01:04:37 (19 frames) and 01:04:55. It never jumps inside the 26.0-52.0 take, and there are no OS or maker marks.
Plate map, 5 s rule. Acceptance: no generated plate runs over 5.0 s, and every join lands on its named cover: 8.9, 22.9, 29.0, 34.0, 38.2, 41.6, 45.0 and 52.0. 50.0 is a hard cut between beats.
Camera-plan ruling, SH02 sign cheat: APPROVED. PR-10 is now spun on its post to face 325° in the world bible, so the cheat belongs to the world. Composite 'STOP' if the letters distort.

Camera-plan ruling, SH10 road-bump join: APPROVED. Acceptance: the bump moves the frame and the car body, with a tire thump on the mic. Jean's head, collar and sunglasses hold within a few pixels relative to the headrest pad (head rule).

Thumb on the icon (B04, B08; V02-B06). Method: a practical plate of the hand double's right thumb (the 6 mm nick) over a blank phone on green, composited over G. Acceptance: it enters nail-side, rests 2.2 s or 1.2 s without a twitch and never presses, so the UI never changes before SC18. Fallback: the script's under-a-second flip, with her eyes on him.
Face reveal, B06. Acceptance: she reads as a deep three-quarter with both eyes, laughing at him, while Jean reads as a lost profile. Risk: the back of her head at the route's first look at her face.
B08 eyes. Acceptance: his face is frontal and centered, and his eyes aim about 5° past the lens toward her, never into it.

Dead eyes (B07-B08; V02-B04/B05). Method: G, locked in composite. Acceptance, tested after degrain: zero blinks and zero eye movement across 45.0-50.0 and 52.0-56.0; lids at the top edge of the iris; dry, dulled corneas; dust on the lashes; hair moving. Fallback: freeze the eye region from the best frame and regrain it with no seam at 100%. A16: first try in the moving car.
Collar touch, B02 (V02-B01). Method: G; the hand is a risk. Acceptance: one hand, two strokes, collar C1 to C2, and his head doesn't move. Fallback: her hand rests on his collar.

Three-step hand chains, B07 and B08. Acceptance: PR-04 hangs by its left arm from her thumb and ring finger across the 45.0 cut and is hooked, lenses out, by 51.0; it never vanishes or doubles. Fallback: already hooked at 50.0.
Vehicle. Method: G. Acceptance: one open 1950s-shape two-seater per LOC-01: left-hand drive, blank rear plate, no badges, no numerals. No other vehicle, person or animal in any frame (A10).
B03 jump cuts. Acceptance: one locked G of Jean over the background plates; head, collar and sunglasses overlay within a few pixels.
Laugh sync, B06 only. Acceptance: laugh peaks land within 2 frames of the torso shakes. One laugh voice across V01, V02 and D01.
Hair in wind: hers is held by the stylist and never crosses the hand shots. His top hair moves as one mass in B07.
No slow motion; everything plays at 24 fps real speed (taste note).
Frame open and close (B06, B08): built in finishing on the phone's own motion. The pillars open in 0.6 s and close in 0.4 s, and the texture switches at the same moment. No dissolve.

Left-index burn: KEEP. A 1 cm glossy oval on the back of the left index finger, applied as makeup on the hand double. Acceptance: present in every frame where the back of her left hand reads (B02, the wheel shots, D01). Fallback: paint it in if a generated plate drops it.

S01 comes from this scene's gold light before B04, shot from behind her right shoulder. Jean is in P1 with his forearm on the door top; the phone shows him under the REC dot; she laughs in three-quarter profile with her eyes on him. This breaks 'hands before faces' on purpose, because a poster needs its lead.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat B10: close on the unbroken dust as she leans over the office step to tug the padlock rather than set a foot on it. She wants proof that nobody has found the motel, and she won't bring him in until she has it. B09 (56-60), to arm herself: she leans across his knees to the glovebox, and her face passes through his open gaze about 50 cm from his eyes. She doesn't look away (casting). She takes the pistol by the grip with the muzzle toward the dash, never over his legs, and seats it grip-up in her right back pocket. Real detail: trained handling, even beside a dead man. B10 (60-64), to check: she walks the frontage alone, glances once at the empty highway, tugs the padlock twice and looks down at the dust. B11 (64-72), to move in: one fast trip with both shoulders loaded and no look back at him, then she shoulders the swollen door. JEAN: P2, still, face turned toward her empty seat. Her lean doesn't move him.
scenes.blocking: LOC-03, last light. Wind comes from the highway (south), and the fronds lean toward the room block. The car is nosed in facing north at x 21.0-22.55, y 13.5-17.5. PR-02 is in the unlocked glovebox (y 76-106), muzzle toward his door. B09: she leans east across his knees, and her head crosses his gaze line about 50 cm in front of his face. The lid drops and stays open. B10: getting out is elided. She walks south-west about 10 m to the office door (x 12, south face) and stops on the gravel, toes off PR-14. The way back is not seen. B11: from the trunk north-east along her worn track to PR-15, on the side his face is turned from. She shoulders the rubbed patch (143-173 cm); the door sticks at 35°, then opens to 90°. Both bags drop just inside the latch-side jamb (LOC-04, x 195-245, y 10-50).
scenes.action_progression: B09, 56.0-60.0, one plate (SH18): engine ping (0.4); she leans across his knees, right hand to the glovebox (0.9); thumbs the latch and the lid drops (0.4); lifts PR-02 by the grip, muzzle toward the dash (0.7); sits back upright (0.8); lifts her right hip and seats it grip-up in her right back pocket, 6 cm showing (0.8). Both hands end free. Hard cut. Hard cut. B11, 64.0-72.0. Plate A (SH20), 64.0-68.0, at the trunk: lid up (0.8); PR-05 onto her left shoulder (1.1); PR-06 onto her right (1.0); both PR-07 sacks hugged to her chest (1.1). The sacks stay at her chest.
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: quick and armed, with one glance at the highway during the walk. Trigger, seen by the camera: the unbroken dust on PR-14. After: she turns back without another look at the road and unloads at speed. She checks nothing else for the rest of the cold open.
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut with a time jump from SC01's phone frame to the full-width carport on 35mm. The engine ping replaces the mic wind.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut on the door scraping open. Her back goes into the dark doorway at frame center, and we cut to the black room inside, where the lantern click lights the wall (SC03). The scrape carries across the cut.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' B11 carries it: she carries his bag beside hers into the room, moving in with him rather than stashing a body. Cut this and the viewer loses that the motel is a home she has kept and checked for the two of them. Without the dust check and the pistol guarding it, the room reads as a trophy lair instead of a house for two.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Pistol PR-02, B09-B10. Method: G. If a practical plate is needed: a non-firing replica under an armorer who checks it before each take and holds it between takes (producer; pending). Acceptance: the muzzle never crosses Jean, crew or the lens; grip up, 6 cm showing against light-wash denim; no markings. Fallback: already in the pocket, no hand on it.

Camera-plan ruling, SH18 vertical jolt: APPROVED only as the car rocking on its springs under her lean. The car and Jean move as one, his head never moves relative to his shoulders, and the jolt never lands during the pistol lift.

Camera-plan ruling, SH20 on the axis: APPROVED. The camera stays south of the car on its centerline, Jean shows only the back of his head, and the open trunk lid never hides the count of two bags and two sacks.
Leaning across the body, B09, a five-step chain. Acceptance: his knees, forearm and head don't move. Risk: he shifts and reads alive.
PR-14. Acceptance: no footprint on the step in any frame of B10 or later.
Carry, B11. Acceptance: exactly two bags and two sacks; nothing appears or vanishes across the 68.0 cut.
PR-12: 'MOTEL' and 'OFFICE' verbatim, composited if garbled; no other text. The loose panel may tick.
Door, B11. Acceptance: two shoves with a stop at 35°, not one swing.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her hands and the chair legs as she drags the second chair up and squares it beside hers. She wants the table set for two. Play her hands. Her head stays above the lantern's pool and never turns to the door (taste note: hands before faces). She unpacks fast, in pairs and handfuls, like someone who has done it many times. When the last jug lands she gives one look, straight across the table at the bare boards where his chair will go. She slows only for the chair, then leaves to bring him in and drags the swollen door shut behind her. The held frame has nobody in it.
scenes.blocking: LOC-04. The held-frame view is from the door end facing wall C; exact placement is the DP's. PR-15 is open at 90°. PR-05 and PR-06 lie at the latch-side jamb (x 195-245, y 10-50), below the held frame. PR-16 is on the table, off, at x 180, y 365. scenes.action_progression: Entry at 72.0: dark room, sacks against her chest. B12, 72.0-82.0.
