Cut into the action at 78.5 as she turns east; the walk to wall D and folding the sacks under PR-17 are elided. Plate C (SH24), 78.5-82.0: PR-19 dragged by its back over the last 0.8 m round the north-east corner (1.0); both hands square it beside PR-18 (0.7); one nudge levels the seat edges (0.3); both hands rest on its back (0.7); she walks south out of frame toward the door, clear by 82.0 (0.8). Hard cut at 82.0. B13, 82.0-88.0 (SH25): a locked hold in which nothing moves. Behind camera, her steps cross the boards (82.0-84.2), then the swollen door scrapes and thuds as she drags it shut from outside (84.2-85.2). From 85.2 there is only the wind pushing at the shut door. B14, 88.0-90.0: the same frame; the LIMERENCE card lands and the wind cuts to silence at 88.0.
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: fast unpacking, hands never pausing. Trigger, seen by the camera: the last jug lands and her head lifts to the bare boards across the table. After: her hands slow. The chair gets 2.7 s against 1.7 s for six cans, with two hands, one nudge and both hands resting 0.7 s on its back, the only rest in the scene. B13-B14 are a hold: the room carries it.
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut from SC02's doorway into the dark room. The door scrape carries across, and the lantern click reveals the wall.
scenes.transition_out: In V01: the LIMERENCE card sits on the held frame in silence, then cut to black at 90.0. In the pilot: a hard cut from the card's silence to SC04's upright phone frame, whose first frame echoes V01-B01's collar and jaw, with Jean alive.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' PR-20 over the table carries it, with PR-19 pulled up beside PR-18: a wall of him alone, none of them together, above a table set for two. Cut this and the viewer loses the gap the idea lives in, and the printer (PR-25) that SC18 pays off.
practical_or_compositing_flags: PR-20 wall (verified fact: none of them together). Method: composite about 40 unique long-lens images of the locked JEAN, tiled to 250 prints on the world bible's grid as a CG texture on the pine. Acceptance at S02 resolution: no print contains a second person; no legible text; Jean in black in every print; the pine at x 280-345 is bare. Risk: a freely generated wall invents couple photos.
Camera-plan ruling, SH22 at the left third: APPROVED. It keeps the bare pine and PR-19's destination clear.

Camera-plan ruling, SH23's head above frame: RETURNED. The head lift at 76.9-77.8 is the scene's only trigger. Smallest fix: her head, in silhouette, is in frame from 76.9 to 77.8 and seen holding on the bare boards; above frame before 76.9 is fine.
Camera-plan ruling, SH24 at 325°: APPROVED. Acceptance: PR-19 ends square beside PR-18 in frame, and her exit clears frame by 82.0.
Camera-plan ruling, the SC03 hard cut at 82.0: APPROVED in place of my body-wipe hidden cut. Acceptance: SH25 is empty from its first frame, and the chair, cans and jugs match SH24.

Door dragged shut, B13. Acceptance: her steps and the scrape and thud are heard behind camera at 82.0-85.2, and nothing in frame moves with them; from 85.2 the wind knocks a shut door in its latch, with no draft in the room. It can't land before the 82.0 cut without cutting the chair's 2.7 s or the head lift; the sound-line change is filed with the writer.

Held frame, B13-B14 and S02. Method: lock the content; the lantern runs on batteries, so nothing flickers. Acceptance, tested after degrain: no motion in props, light, dust or photos across 82.0-90.0, then live grain and gate weave back over the whole frame.
Unpacking across the 74.9 cut. Acceptance: the counts hold (6 cans, 2 full jugs, 5 oranges, 1 printer, 9 empty jugs); nothing lands without a hand or the cut placing it; nothing is sped up.
Title: LIMERENCE only, final 2 s, silent, composited. S02 is the B13 frame with no text.

scenes.performance_beats: No new performance: V02 is rebuilt from SC01's plates. It stays Venus's piece, seen through her phone. Hero beat V02-B06: her thumb rests on the flip icon over his open eyes, then slides back. It has to read with the sound off.
scenes.blocking: Native 9:16. The phone-frame plates (B01, B02, B04-B06) are the upright frame at full height, with nothing restaged, generated at 1080x1920 or better. B03 is cut from V01-B07's two setups: 42.8-43.8, the medium two-shot as the frame is drawn forward off his face, toward the lens, and 45.0-46.0, the close on his head passing dead ahead. Her hand and his face sit in the middle third of both, and the lift travels toward the lens, not across the frame, so the crop holds it. B04 is a static punch-in on the B08 eyes plate: no push.
scenes.action_progression: B01, 0.0-1.5: V01 5.5-7.0, the brush and the collar, REC 00:06:13. B02, 1.5-4.0: V01 15.3-17.8, scrub hills, REC 00:52:30. B03, 4.0-6.0: V01 42.8-43.8, then a jump to 45.0-46.0; 35mm texture, no UI. B04, 6.0-9.0: a handle from the B08 eyes plate, punched in so his eyes fill the frame from its first frame, and still; REC 01:04:55. B05, 9.0-11.0: the laugh shake, REC 01:04:58. B06, 11.0-13.0 (V02-SH07), REC 01:05:00: the thumb enters nail-side on f0 and lands on the icon (0.3); rests over his eyes (1.2); slides back (0.4); the mic cuts (0.1). B07, 13.0-15.0: black, the REC dot gone, LIMERENCE centered, silent.
scenes.emotional_shift: The same shift as SC01, compressed. Before: care (the collar) and time (the timer jump). Trigger: his open eyes under the light (B04). After: her laugh shakes the frame while his eyes stay still (B05), and her thumb rests and retreats (B06). With the sound off, the timer and the unblinking eyes carry time and death, and the thumb carries the want.
scenes.transition_in: Opens straight on the phone frame mid-action at the collar, with wind on the mic from frame one.
scenes.transition_out: The recording stops: hard cut to black at 13.0 with the mic wind cut dead, then LIMERENCE in silence to 15.0.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' B06 carries it: her thumb on the flip icon over his open eyes, sliding back. Cut it and V02 becomes a dead-body reveal; the want, and the reason to open V01, are gone.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Camera-plan ruling, no push in V02-B04: APPROVED. B04 is a static punch-in. Acceptance: at the punched size the dull corneas and the dust on the lashes hold, so generate the eyes plate at 4K equivalent. If the eye-freeze fallback is used, it passes the no-seam test at that size.
Camera-plan ruling, V02-SH07 thumb entering on f0: APPROVED. Acceptance: the thumb is moving on B06's first frame, rests 1.2 s without a twitch, and never presses.

Footage length. V01-B08's phone section runs 4.0 s, and B04-B06 need about 7 s on his eyes. Method: generate the eyes plate with handles (two plates of up to 5 s joined on a laugh jolt) and shoot the thumb plate long. Acceptance: no frame used twice.
B03 crop. Acceptance: in both source windows her hand, the glasses and his face stay inside the middle third; the lift reads as the frame coming off his face toward the lens.
Teaser clock. Acceptance: the timer runs continuously within each beat on the script's teaser values, deliberately not frame-matched to V01.
Muted read. Acceptance: with the sound off, a test viewer reads 'a man who never wakes, and she won't turn the camera on herself'. The REC timer and the title are the only text.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her hands as the pistol goes into the glovebox and the tin comes out. She wants to go in before he leaves alone again, and walking into his frame means going without the gun. Tactic 1: starting from V01-B01's collar-and-jaw framing, she zooms toward his face until the lens runs out and the picture breaks into grain, and she keeps it there. Real detail: she'd rather have his face soft than the room sharp. Tactic 2: she waits while he raises two fingers for another. Trigger: the BARTENDER sets the tab slip face down in front of him, and she moves at once, tidying as she goes. Nothing is left on the seat, the glovebox is locked, the curtain goes on. Jean's living face stays soft and grainy inside her phone, a picture rather than a performance shot.
scenes.blocking: LOC-01, top up. The passenger curtain is fitted; the driver's curtain is off, stowed behind her seat. The car is parked at the far curb, driver's side to the bar at 14 m. VENUS in the driver seat: PR-01 upright in her right hand at the open side; PR-02 grip-up in her right back pocket; PR-61 key 1 in the ignition. PR-08 (band on) lies on the passenger cushion with PR-09 half under it; PR-03 is closed in the glovebox. Through the window (LOC-05 wall A, x 40-440): JEAN on stool 2 (y 350), PR-04 hooked in his placket, PR-33 at x 148, y 395, PR-05 under the stool; the BARTENDER in the aisle. She gets out of the driver door (street side, facing the bar) and crosses to the glazed door (x 470-560).

She zooms until his face breaks into grain (4.0) and holds (to about 0:40). A 1.5 s insert of PR-09. He raises two fingers and is poured another (to about 1:00). scenes.transition_in: Hard cut from V01's silent card. The first frame repeats V01-B01's framing (upright phone frame, REC dot, black collar and jaw) with him alive. Muffled bar noise and street sound come in on the cut.
scenes.transition_out: Cut on action: her hand hits the bar door's glass from outside, and SC05 opens inside as the door swings in, with Jean's back in the foreground. Street sound becomes bar room tone.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' PR-08 and the lowered phone carry it: months of him alone, all shot from behind her lens, and then she puts the phone away and walks into his frame. Cut this and the viewer loses where the wall came from and the first time she steps out from behind the camera toward him.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Her phone screen. Method: a practical plate of Jean through real bar glass, with the UI and grainy zoom composited. Acceptance: the UI matches V01 exactly, and Jean stays readable through the reflections at the end of the zoom (soft is fine, lost is not).
PR-09. Acceptance: only 'NO CHARGES FILED' is legible, in one 1.5 s insert; no agency, seal or case number; fictional (A02).

Pistol, tin and key chain. Method: practical, a non-firing replica under an armorer who checks it before each take and holds it between takes (producer; pending). Acceptance: the muzzle never crosses her, crew or the lens, with no crew or camera on the passenger side for the lay-in. The tin is never opened. The report folds and nothing is left on the cushion.
PR-08. Acceptance: no text, plates or storefront names in any print that reads.
Street. Acceptance: no legible brand, plate or sign (A10).

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on the straw as her fingertip lays the first one in the wet ring his glass left. She wants him to agree to her game; JEAN wants to finish his drink without being seen. 'Have we met before?' is a test she already knows the answer to. Play it straight: she is listening for a lie. He tells the truth, and she gives nothing away. Her phone stays in her right chest pocket all scene and her hand never goes to it. It is the first time she sits in his frame with no lens between them. The Naked and Famous joke lands with her right hand on his forearm and a real laugh, and we cut on the laugh. JEAN starts rounded over his glass, elbow on the worn patch. The mimosa jab gets to him: he props himself up and turns his stool to her. BARTENDER: eyes on the tab, 'What can I get you guys?' said half to the counter. Real detail: Jean slides the tab slip back unsigned with one finger, without looking at it.
scenes.blocking: LOC-05. VENUS comes in by the glazed door (wall A, x 470-560) and walks north behind the stools, behind Jean's back, to stool 3 (y 440). She turns the stool fully to him and keeps her elbows off the counter. JEAN is on stool 2 (y 350) with PR-05 underneath. PR-29 stands at x 130, y 480 by her elbow. Jean lifts PR-33 off x 148, y 395 and sets it at x 140, y 320, away from her, leaving the wet ring between them. She lays the base straw through the ring at x 148, y 385-405. scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her right thumb as it rests on the flip-camera icon and this time presses, and the screen shows both of them. She wants to get into one photograph with him. Her thumb rests as it did twice in the car. Trigger: she lifts her head from his shoulder, looks round past the back of his head at the next man's two prints she has just pinned, and holds: the wall has already moved on. She turns back, lays her head on his shoulder again and presses. For the first time her eyes go into a lens, her own front camera, and she is smiling. Two of her left fingers lift toward his chin and stop short. She doesn't touch him, doesn't lower the phone and plays no disappointment; the smile holds and she takes the photo, then taps print. Once she sits, she takes her hair down, and her curls fall loose onto his black shoulder before her head goes there. JEAN: the head-alone rule; his face stays where she set it at dusk, eyes open, no blink.

scenes.emotional_shift: Before: her thumb rests on the icon (1.2 s), as it did twice in the car. Trigger, seen by the camera: she lifts her head, turns past the back of his head to the next man's two prints, and holds 1.0 s. After: she turns back, lays her head on his shoulder again and presses. The press is the change: her own face on her screen, eyes in the lens, smiling. Second beat, a hold: her fingers stop short of his chin, his gaze passes wide of the lens, and she takes the picture with no change of face.
scenes.transition_in: Match cut from SC17: seated in black in the white chair becomes seated in black under the wall, with the wind at the door.
scenes.transition_out: End of the pilot. Hard cut to black at the end of the final wide; the wind carries over the black.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' Her first press of the flip icon, and PR-27 pinned between Jean's wall and the next man's, carry it. Cut this and the viewer loses the answer to every thumb rest: she wanted one picture with him and gets it only when he can't look. They also lose the setup the series repeats.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Front-camera screen. Method: composite the UI; the print control is an original icon with no text, in the A10 package. Acceptance: the lantern lights her face, her eyes are in the lens, and his eyes read off to his left, past and below it.

Phone placement. Acceptance: in the front-camera frame both his eyes read, and they never meet the lens or look down at the screen. If a take shows his eyes meeting the lens, move the phone; never re-pose his head.

Pistol PR-02, draw and drop into the bag. Method: practical, a non-firing replica under an armorer who checks it before each take and holds it between takes (producer; pending). Acceptance: the muzzle points down through the draw, never crosses Jean, crew or the lens, and lies toward wall B in the bag, below the held frame. It never goes on the table.
Fingers toward his chin. Acceptance: they stop about 2 cm short; there is no contact and no nod. The head-alone rule holds.

Hair down. Acceptance: she is seated before the elastics come out; both go into her right front pocket, and the curls fall across his black shoulder before her head lands. No hair crosses the phone's lens or his eyes in the front-camera frame (stylist confirms VENUS_L03's fall).

Printer whir. Method: a practical unit, never sped up. Acceptance: the whir starts 1.0 s after her thumb taps print, so it has a visible cause. If the unit runs longer or shorter than 35.0 s, the final wide absorbs the difference and never runs under 15 s.
PR-27 insert, 3.5 s. Acceptance: the card-size print reads between Jean's grid and PR-28, clearly smaller than the 15 x 10 prints; PR-27 is pre-printed from the actual frame.
Final wide. Acceptance, tested after degrain: nothing moves but her breathing, then live grain and gate weave over the whole frame.
Dead eyes: the V01 makeup lock, no blink.

evidence.specificity: All six earlier notes are fixed, and a storyboard artist or cinematographer can now work second by second. The SC10 to SC12 timing is resolved: "SC12 0.0 = SC11 33.0 ... tap running at SC11 32.5-34.0; track start at SC11 33.3 = SC12 0.3; ice at 40.5 = 7.5; door at 55.5 = 22.5. The bedroom-to-kitchen walk is 6.5 s." The climax is written as actions that can be timed: "100.4-101.4: her right hand leaves the sheet and passes over PR-01 without slowing to the ring (1.0). 101.4-103.4: turns the ring to about 80% (2.0)." A few gaps remain. The SC04 trigger ("the tab slip lands in her frame") happens while her phone is zoomed on his face to grain, so a storyboard artist would have to ask how the slip gets into that frame. One piece of the B07 geometry is also still open (see notes).
evidence.distinctiveness: Nobody else's project could use this. The route's rest-and-slide gesture runs through the whole pilot in physical form. SC07: "Her fingertip rests on its top (1.0) and slides off (0.5); it stays ... the flip-icon gesture, made while he is alive, on the one straw he stood up for them." SC10 adds a new version: "steps back to the distance she holds her phone at, and looks at them, the phone in her hand and not raised." SC11 plants a gesture for the ending: "he flattens his own collar points in the mirror with two fingers, the gesture she will make on him dead." The SC18 trigger ("she lifts her head, turns past the back of his head to the next man's two prints, and holds 1.0 s") could only belong to this series.
evidence.fit: Every must-include is staged and every must-avoid has an acceptance test. The SC08 fix keeps the route's payoff whole: "Acceptance: her thumb never touches PR-35's flip icon; the screen faces Jean for the whole shot," so SC18 stays the first press. The meds are handled as the brief requires: "There is no wince and no pause on the full compartments or the date, so the meds are seen and never the reason." The tin stays shut until his line: "the camera stays south of the raised lid and no higher than its top edge." There is no slow motion and no VO, and brands and the armorer are left pending. SC11's weak link to the route is filed honestly as a writer blocker with the smallest fix, which is what the craft brief asks for.
evidence.craft: The sub-steps add up and the continuity holds almost everywhere. SC01: "Plate 41.6-45.0 ... (0.4) ... (0.8) ... (1.6) ... (0.6)" and "Plate map, 5 s rule. Acceptance: no generated plate runs over 5.0 s, and every join lands on its named cover." The SC16 roll works physically: "she pulls, and he rolls onto his back toward her, dead weight, his right arm coming over onto the sheet between them (2.0)." I checked it: pulling the far shoulder rolls a prone man through his near side onto his back, which brings that far arm over, as written. The SC18 phone bearing ("about 57° wide of the lens") checks out against the table layout. It falls short of 9 on a few points. The new B07 pull direction ("draws the frame north along the pad toward the windshield") runs perpendicular to the pad, so it cannot free a pinned arm without lifting his head. The SC10 click flag contradicts the scene's own transition. The intimacy and stunt coordinators appear in the flags but are never filed as pending with the producer.

notes.target: SC01 / V01-B07, plate 41.6-45.0 (the glasses lift) and the 45.0-46.8 head turn
notes.note: In P1 the pad is behind his head to the south, and PR-04's right arm lies east-west between his right temple and the pad, pinned by the weight of his head. The restaged pull goes north, toward the windshield, which is straight off the pad. That pulls the pinned arm into his temple and lifts his head, which is exactly the drag the acceptance forbids. The last round's wording ('forward along the pad toward the windshield') caused this, so it is a correction, not a new requirement. The arm can only come out lengthwise. Keep 1.6 s and re-split it: her fingers at the left hinge lift the left arm off his left ear, pivoting the frame on the trapped hinge (0.6); she draws the frame straight out the way his face points, toward his door, about 12 cm, so the right arm slides out lengthwise from between temple and pad (0.6); she brings it back past his face on the windshield side, toward the lens (0.4). Keep 'his head holds against the pad; the only movement is the lenses clearing his face.' Then check that V02-B03's 42.8-43.8 window keeps the 12 cm cross-frame move inside the middle third. If it doesn't, move that window onto the 0.4 s return. The alternative is to make the CG PR-04 the primary method instead of the fallback. Also add an acceptance line for the 120° turn: the camera sits inside the sweep, so his eyes cross the lens axis mid-turn. They cross only while the head is moving and settle at least 10° west of the lens, and no frame with the head stopped has them in it (casting: 'aimed past the lens and never into it').
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Stage around what models get wrong'; 'Start and end each action on a holdable state'; quality bar craft: 'nothing physically implausible'; A16; the treatment's own head-alone acceptance

looks.garment_silhouette: Closet: mid-to-high tier, bought plain and kept for years. She spends on fit, deep pockets and boots, never on a name. A tailor recut her jeans' back pockets to men's size. She dresses in the whites of her apartment plus pale denim. Story: Thursday 22 October 2026 (from PR-36's date, assumed), SC04-SC10. The city is at about 19 °C at night, so the jacket is on and open and her ankles are covered. She changes off screen in SC11 and hangs the jacket on PR-62, and she never wears it again in the pilot. Head to toe: a bone moleskin jacket, single-breasted, 4 buttons worn open, small point collar. It is waist length, with the hem level all round 1 cm above the top of the jeans waistband. It has two pockets: a right chest welt for the phone (PR-01) and an inside left pocket for the tin (PR-03). The sleeves are cut to mid-forearm with a 4 cm turned-back cuff. Under it is a chalk jersey shell with a high round neck, sleeveless with 7 cm shoulders, tucked in. Pale-blue high-rise bootcut jeans, full length, with a matched pair of oversized back pockets. A brown-black belt shows below the jacket hem. Brown-black pull-on ankle boots: 4 cm stacked heel, almond toe, shaft 3 cm above the ankle bone, worn under the jeans. Ecru ankle socks and an unlined bra, both hidden. Older than the story: the jeans.
looks.materials_colors: Jacket: cotton moleskin 330 g/m², brushed face, matte, holds its shape; bone #D6CCBA (approx L*82, C*9). The fronts are half-lined in cotton drill 200 g/m², natural #D8CFBE, and the facings are moleskin. Buttons: bone corozo #D2C7B2, matte. Right chest welt: a 2 cm welt in the moleskin over a drill bag, with both lower corners bar-tacked. Behind it, the right chest is interfaced with 110 g/m² cotton fusible from the shoulder seam to 2 cm below the bag. Two 1 cm cotton twill stay tapes, natural #D8CFBE, run from the bag's top corners to the shoulder seam. Inside left pocket: a welt set across the facing and lining, over a drill bag bar-tacked at both bottom corners. Hanging loop: 5 cm of drill tape, #D8CFBE, at the inside back neck, for PR-62. A flat 80 g chain weight sits in each front's hem facing. Shell: cotton-silk single jersey 160 g/m², solid, chalk #EEE9DF (approx L*93). Plain jersey, because a fine rib would moiré and fight the 35mm grain. Jeans: rigid 100% cotton denim 12.5 oz/yd², light stonewash, pale blue #8FA3B8 (approx L*66, C*13, h 260°), as LOC-03 asks, sewn in tonal ecru thread. Back pockets: a matched pair, each with a single row of ecru topstitching around the edge and bar-tacked top corners. No decorative stitching, patch or tab. Hidden inside the right one is a sling in cotton drill 200 g/m², natural #D8CFBE (see fit). Front scoop pockets and bags as in VENUS_L03. Rivets and shank button are unstamped, gunmetal #5B5D60 approx, satin. Older than the story: the right back pocket is faded to #A9B9C9 in an L, the outline of the part of PR-02 that rides inside it. The L is a 17 x 3.5 cm band (the slide) whose lower edge runs 6 cm below the mouth, joined at the side-seam end by a 7 x 2.5 cm block rising to the mouth (the lower grip). The mouth is frayed to white threads for 8 cm at that end, where the grip rubs. To rebuild it, mask the L, sand and bleach-rub it, and sand the edge. It is a detail, not an identity mark, because models mirror. Belt: 3 cm bridle leather, brown-black #2E2724 (approx L*16, C*4), 5 holes, with a roller buckle in blackened steel #2F3032 approx, matte. Boots: calf leather, brown-black #2E2724, hidden elastic gore, no hardware; toes scuffed and re-polished, dark sole edge, no coloured sole. Socks: cotton, ecru #E4DED2. Bra: unlined, tan-brown #9C6A4C approx, matched to her skin. No logo, lettering or trade dress on any piece.
looks.fit_notes: 177 cm, US women's 4/S, tall sleeve. Jacket: shoulder seam at the shoulder point, 10 cm ease at the chest. The fronts hang straight and open, 2 cm off the shell. The hem sits 1 cm above the waistband top and 7 cm above the back-pocket mouths. Right chest welt: a 9 cm horizontal opening, its top edge level with the armhole base (22 cm above the hem), centred 10 cm in from the front edge. The bag is 13.5 cm deep and 10 cm wide and ends 8.5 cm above the hem. From SC04 (as she leaves the car) to SC10, PR-01 (15 x 7.2 x 0.8 cm, about 200 g assumed) rides upright, screen-in, lens end down; its top 1.5 cm of bare black glass and frame shows above the welt (PR-01 S2). The stay tapes carry the weight to the shoulder, so the right front hangs plumb, its hem stays level with the left to within 1 cm, and the welt stays horizontal. Inside left pocket: the welt is 14 cm wide, 2 cm above the armhole base; the bag is 22 cm deep and ends 2 cm above the hem. PR-03 rides at the bottom; from SC08 the 20 cm PR-30 stands beside it, its top 2 cm under the welt. Phone and tin sit on opposite fronts, outside right and inside left, and never share a pocket. The jacket ends above her lap, so no sit fold crosses either pocket on the bar stool or in the rideshare, and the straw reaches SC12 uncreased. In SC09 his hands go in through the open fronts to the inside left pocket; the outside right welt stays shut on the phone. Cuff: the edge sits 12 cm above the wrist bone, so both wrists and hands read, and so do her three locked marks (right-hand scar, right-thumb nick, left-index burn): the SC05 forearm touch, the SC07 chimney and the S03 fingertip. In S03 no cuff comes within 30 cm of the straw house. Shell: 4 cm ease, neckline 2 cm below the collarbone notch. Jeans: 4 cm waistband with its top 2 cm below the navel, 2 cm ease at the hip, fitted through the thigh. Bootcut from the knee to a 23 cm opening; the hem sits 1.5 cm off the floor at the heel. Back pockets: each 19 cm wide x 15 cm deep, mouths 6 cm below the waistband top, inner edges 2 cm from the centre-back seam. Right pocket: a drill sling spans the full inner width with its bottom fold 6 cm below the mouth, its sides caught in the pocket's edge topstitching and its top under the pocket hem, so nothing new shows outside. PR-02 (17 x 12 x 3 cm, about 600 g, both assumed) rides slide down along the sling fold, grip up at the side-seam end, muzzle toward the centre back. 6 cm of grip stands above the mouth, its top level with the waistband top and 1 cm under the jacket hem, so the grip clears the jacket seated or reaching back (PR-02 S1). The bar tacks and belt carry the weight, so the waistband doesn't dip on the right. Belt on its middle hole in every look. The boots add 4 cm: she stands 181 cm, about 5 cm under JEAN in his shoes.
accessories: Nothing worn. Ears, neck, wrists and both hands bare: no ring, watch or bracelet. Her hands touch the phone, his forearm, the straws and the tin (taste note: hands before faces).
Nails bare and short: 1-2 mm free edge, filed square, buffed.
Hand double (casting joint lock): the same bare nails, the three marks transferred, the same cuff landmark.

Set-owned: PR-01 in the right chest welt from SC04 to SC10 (set on PR-53 off screen in SC11). PR-03 in the inside left pocket, joined by PR-30 from SC08. PR-02 on the right back pocket's sling until the SC04 swap into the glovebox.
Car keys (PR-61) in the left front jeans pocket from SC04. No bag, no sunglasses.

looks.garment_silhouette: Closet: the one thing at home she has worn for years. Story: SC12 into SC17, the apartment at about 21 °C, night into morning. She does all of SC16-SC17's labour in it: rolling JEAN over, pulling the fitted corner, dressing him, stripping and remaking the bed, kneeling to scrub PR-45. Change beat: after the flat straw lands on the pink cloth in PR-60 and before she closes the tin, she changes off screen into VENUS_L03. Head to toe: one oversized men's athletic T-shirt with raglan sleeves to the elbow and a crew collar rib with a V-notch at centre front, 81 cm from the high point of the shoulder to the front hem (80 cm at the back). Under it a skin-matched modesty short, never seen. Bare legs and bare feet. The raglan line and V-notch make it read as a gym or team shirt in a wide. Which team (Lucas's Raptors shirt) stays open until A10 clears it or a fictional team is designed and cleared (blocker 5). No team colour, logo, number or lettering. Older than the story: the T-shirt.
looks.materials_colors: Combed cotton single jersey 180 g/m², solid, garment-washed. Body: ecru #E8E3D8 (approx L*90, C*4). Raglan sleeves, collar rib and V-notch: oatmeal #D2C9B7 (approx L*81, C*9, h 84°), so the diagonal from underarm to collar reads in a wide. Raglan seams twin-needle coverstitched in tonal ecru thread. Collar: 2 cm 1x1 rib with a 4 cm V-notch insert. No mesh, because it moirés. Older than the story: more than 100 washes. The collar rib ripples, the side seams twist 2 cm toward the front, and the front hem hangs 1 cm longer than the back. To rebuild it, enzyme-wash the tee and stretch the rib by hand. A second tee, aged the same way, stands by for SC17. Modesty short (production only): circular-knit nylon-elastane 190 g/m², no side seams, bonded edges, #9C6A4C approx to her skin. SC17 risk: PR-46 turns pink #E3A9A6, and cotton jersey takes the stain on contact and won't come clean between takes. Rule broken on purpose: the craft rule asks for a colour set apart from the set. Both tones sit 5-14 L* under the walls #F4F2EE and the sheets #F8F7F4, so she belongs to the white room, her skin and dark curls carry her read, and JEAN stays the only dark mass (verified: 'The colour theme is white'; tone: clean). Story-red check (no product): the drops #6E1C18 are approx L*24, C*43, h 34°. Ecru clears by chroma at C*4; oatmeal clears at C*9 and sits 50° away.
looks.fit_notes: A men's XL tall on a US women's 4. Raglan sleeves, so no shoulder seam: the sleeve line runs from the underarm to the collar, and the cloth drops past her shoulder point. The oversized neck drops the garment's high point 2 cm below hers. 40 cm ease at the chest. The V-notch point sits 2 cm below the collarbone notch. The sleeve hem sits at the elbow, so both forearms and hands read: SC12 with the two glasses and her fingertip on the tin lid, SC15 folding his clothes and turning the speaker ring, SC16 her hand to her forehead and the roll, SC17 dressing him and scrubbing. Hem states, fit-checked on her (the hem is taken up or let down to hold the standing mark). Standing: front hem 10 cm above the top of the kneecap. Seated in PR-44 (SC12-SC13): about 20 cm above the kneecap across the lap. Carried (SC14): up to the hip crease on the outer thigh. Bent over the bed or kneeling forward to scrub (SC16-SC17): the back hem rises to the gluteal fold. The modesty short is cut for the worst of these, rise to the natural waist, legs ending 4 cm below the gluteal fold, so the garment, not the hem, keeps 'no nudity in any piece'; if its bonded edge enters frame it reads as skin. Lucas's 'no underwear' is implied, never shown. In bed (SC15-SC16) the tee stays on under the duvet.
accessories: Nothing worn. Ears, neck, wrists, hands and feet bare.
Nails as VENUS_L01: bare and short.

She leaves carrying the bone jacket, never wearing it, the tin in its inside left pocket (PR-03 S6). V01, V02 and S01: the open car, 27 °C in the late afternoon falling to 17 °C at dusk; no jacket, sleeves rolled because she is driving and filming. SC18: the motel at night, about 15 °C; only her hair changes. looks.fit_notes: Shirt: shoulder seam at the shoulder point, 12 cm ease at the chest. Tucked 10 cm deep, so it stays in when she leans across JEAN's knees (V01-B09) and walks the frontage (B10). Unrolled, the sleeves end at the wrist bone. Two 6 cm turns put the roll's lower edge 12 cm above the wrist bone, the L01 cuff landmark, so the right-hand scar, right-thumb nick and left-index burn read the same at the bar and in the car. Hand double: the same roll and landmark, nails bare, marks transferred. Neckline open down to the third button at the sternum. From the first second of V01-B08, one open arm of PR-04 hooks over the placket edge above that button, lenses outside the shirt, until she unhooks it in SC18. Belt on its middle hole. Front pockets: scoop mouth 11 cm along the waistband and 8 cm down the side seam; bag 19 cm deep from the waistband top and 14 cm wide, its fly-side edge carried into a stay stitched into the fly, so a load hangs across the front instead of dragging the waistband. Clear zone: no cuff, hair or strap enters the lower-right 15% of the phone frame; only her thumb does.

Nails bare, short, filed square. The right-hand scar, right-thumb nick and left-index burn stay uncovered.

looks.garment_silhouette: Closet: mid-price and bought to be looked at. He spends on the shirt and the shoes and skimps on the trousers and belt, which he hasn't replaced since he got heavier. Everything he is ever photographed in is black. Story: Thursday 22 into Friday 23 October 2026 (assumed), SC04-SC15. The city is at about 19 °C at night and the bar and apartment are warm: one black outfit, no jacket. Head to toe: a black long-sleeve dress shirt, semi-spread collar on a 4 cm stand, no chest pocket, 7 buttons, top button open and the second fastened, cuffs buttoned, tucked in all round. Black flat-front trousers, mid rise, straight leg, half break. A brown-black belt on hole 1, nearest the buckle. Black mid-calf socks. Brown-black leather Derbies (PR-41). Plain black boxer briefs. SC15: clothes off (PR-56), bare back and arms, the white sheet at his waist. Older than the story: the belt. K08 wall-print rail (PR-08, PR-20: about 250 prints, June to October 2026, assumed), three variants that date the prints. K08-A, about 100 prints (40%), night bar-window and night street: this look (SH-1, TR-1, belt, PR-41) without the third-night creases; PR-08's top print, at the bar window, is K08-A. K08-B, about 100 prints (40%), June to August day prints at the pump and crossing streets: a black heavyweight crew tee, sleeves to mid-bicep, worn untucked over TR-1, black socks, PR-41. K08-C, about 50 prints (25 day, 25 dusk), October: a black hip-length overshirt worn open over the K08-B tee, with TR-1 and PR-41. That gives PR-20's half night, half day.
looks.materials_colors: Shirt (SH-1): unmercerised cotton twill 150 g/m², lightly brushed, true matte, blue-black #24262B (approx L*15, C*4, h 276°). The nap holds PR-57's dust, so the grains, not the cloth, glint under the video light. Risk: the same nap grabs white bouclé fibre from the sofa, PR-44 and the rug, so shirt and trousers are lint-rolled between takes. Collar band 43 cm; the stays are gone. Buttons: matte black corozo #26272B. Trousers (TR-1): cotton-stretch twill 280 g/m², matte, blue-black #25272C (approx L*16), in the shirt's cast so the two read as one mass (verified: 'The man is dressed in all black, as her black hole'). Boxer briefs: cotton-modal jersey, black #232428, plain waistband, no lettering. Socks: cotton-nylon, black #232427. Belt: 3 cm cowhide, brown-black #2A2624 (approx L*16), 5 holes 2.5 cm apart, buckle in matte black oxide #2B2C2E approx. Older than the story: a deep crease with cracked grain at the middle (third) hole, where it fastened before he got heavier, and the tip worn pale #5A4A40. To rebuild it, bend and sand the leather. Derbies (PR-41): calf leather, brown-black #2A2624, stitched welt, black sole edge, no coloured sole, no logo. Third-night state, SC04-SC15: worn since the morning and sat in at the bar since early evening. The collar points have gone soft, tips lifted 6-8 mm off the shirt front; horizontal crumple creases at both inner elbows; a fan of sit creases across the trouser lap. There is no sharp fold line anywhere: the fold creases are JEAN_L02's, made by her. To rebuild: stays out, the actor sits in SH-1 and TR-1 for 40 minutes with his elbows bent before the first take, and the steamer never touches the elbows or the lap. K08-B tee: cotton single jersey 240 g/m², solid, matte, blue-black #26282D (approx L*16). K08-C overshirt: brushed cotton drill 300 g/m², solid, blue-black #292B30 (approx L*17), point collar, 5 matte black corozo buttons #26272B, two patch hip pockets, no chest pocket. Bar-set risk: #24262B (approx L*15) on the counter #3A2418 (approx L*17, C*15, h 54°) inside the #1A120D room (approx L*6). Value alone won't separate him from the counter. The costume gives his blue cast about 140° from the room's brown-black (weak at C*4), matte brushed twill against the counter's satin varnish, the collar edge with its lifted points and the wedge of deep skin at the open neck, and from SC05 Venus's bone jacket #D6CCBA (approx L*82) beside him. The rest is the DP's. The route's #111111 is the graded read; in a neutral grade the fabric is #24262B. Nothing branded.
looks.fit_notes: 184 cm, US men's L, 36 waist. Shirt: shoulder seam at the shoulder point. Top button open, so the collar stand sits 1-2 cm clear of his neck and the soft points spread and lift. Cuffs at the wrist bone. Tucked 10 cm deep; the front blouses 2 cm over the belt where his belly sits. The button line pulls across the belly but never gapes: a hidden snap sits between the 4th and 5th buttons. Third-night creases land in a 10 cm band at each inner elbow and across the trouser lap from the hip crease to mid-thigh, and they still show standing (SC08 exit, SC10). Trousers: waist 3 cm below the navel and snug (he has outgrown them), 20 cm leg opening, half break on the Derbies, room in the seat to lift and carry VENUS (SC14). Belt on hole 1, 5 cm out from the old crease. SC10: shoes off on the mat (PR-41 S2), socks on. SC15: under the sheet, a skin-matched modesty garment (#6E4631 approx), never seen; the sheet sits at the waist. K08-B tee: shoulder seam at the point, 8 cm ease, hem at the hip, covering the belt. K08-C overshirt: shoulder seam 1 cm past the point, sleeves to the wrist bone, hem at the hip bone, fronts hanging open. Builds SH-1 and TR-1 are listed under JEAN_L02.
accessories: Placket bare SC04-SC15: nothing hooked, clipped or tacked to it. PR-04 is not on him; it rides in PR-05's outside pocket until SC17 (film director's ruling; set-owned; blocker 1).

assumptions: Date and season follow PR-36's timestamp (10/23/2026 01:47, itself marked ASSUMED): the bar night is Thursday 22 October 2026 and the drive is Friday 23 October, US Southwest. Assumed temperatures: city at night about 19 °C, apartment 21 °C, desert 27 °C falling to 17 °C at dusk, motel at night about 15 °C.

PR-04 ruling, quoted. It was issued by the film director in the package review returned with the previous version of this look sheet; the note carries no date. Target: 'JEAN_L01 accessories (PR-04 hooked in the placket) and its SC04-SC15 continuity lock'. Text: 'Ruling: the sunglasses stay in the duffel's outside pocket until SC17, which is where the world bible, script SC17 and treatment SC17 already put them. Remove the placket hook, the thread tack, the SC15 "folded on top of his shirt" state and the lock line.' The director cites 'World bible PR-04 S0 and PR-56 ("Nothing hangs from the shirt placket in SC04-SC15"); treatment SC17 ("PR-04 out of its outside pocket"); style bible blocker 1'. The world bible in the package I was given says the opposite (PR-04 S0: placket hook and thread tack; PR-05: 'No outside pocket'), and the script's SC17 says only 'puts his sunglasses on him'. I follow the director's ruling and log the mismatch as blocker 1.

Other IDs I use, all quoted from the same film-director package-review note, which cites 'Style bible JEAN_L02 hair and builds; camera plan SH14 and SH19'. K08 is the kit sheet that 'drives every print on the V01/S02 wall'. SH14 and SH19 are the practical plates in the camera plan. CHR-JEAN-DEAD@v1 is the generated dead-Jean reference the double is approved against. The camera plan, the K08 sheet and that reference are not in the package I was given, so I use the IDs as quoted and cannot check them.

The next man in PR-28 has a proposed look, PR28_MAN_L01, kept out of the looks list: the checker accepts only casting-bible IDs, and he has none (blocker 7). He is the fictional man on the courthouse steps in two daylight prints, matching no real person or case. October 2026, about 22 °C. Closet: one suit, bought off the rack for court, a size loose. Head to toe: a mid-grey two-piece suit, single-breasted, 2 buttons, jacket buttoned at the top button, hip length, trousers with a full break; a white shirt, collar open at the top button, no tie; dark brown lace-ups. Colours: suit in wool worsted 260 g/m², mid-grey #7E7F80 (approx L*53, C*1). That is 38 L* above Jean's #24262B, and at C*1 it sits well off the paneling #7A5A3C (approx L*41, C*24, h 68°). Shirt: cotton poplin 115 g/m², white #EDEBE5 (approx L*93). Shoes: leather, dark brown #4A3528. Plain unmarked fabric throughout. Fit: jacket shoulder seam 1 cm past the shoulder point; sleeves to the wrist bone, no shirt cuff showing. Hair: straight, mid-brown #5A4535 approx (pending casting), 3 cm on top, a hard side part, combed flat to the skull; clean-shaven. Skin depth and undertone must come from casting. Locks: [each PR-28 print] the grey suit buttoned over a white open collar, no tie: grey and white are the only two blocks, with nothing black above the shoes. [each PR-28 print] Hair flat to the skull with the side part on the same side in both prints; no beard, no sunglasses.

Third-night wear on SH-1 and TR-1 (soft lifted collar tips, crumples at both inner elbows, sit creases across the lap) holds from SC04 to SC15. The creases carry into JEAN_L02 because the clothes are never pressed. What she adds is visibly different: sharp fold creases, the fastened top button and flat collar points. The K08-A prints show SH-1 without the third-night creases, because they are earlier nights.

The K08 dates (June to October 2026) and shares (K08-A about 100 prints, K08-B about 100, K08-C about 50) are assumed. They fill PR-08's 'going back months' and PR-20's 'about half night, half day' within the ~250 count the world bible assumes. The wall's grid order and which print sits where belong to production design.
Jean's black: the world bible carries #24262B for PR-56 and #2A2624 for PR-41. The route's #111111 stays the graded read for the colourist. All K08 blacks sit at approx L*15-17 in the same blue cast.

Pocket carries: a matched pair of 19 x 15 cm back pockets, with a drill sling in the right one whose fold sits 6 cm below the mouth, so 6 cm of grip shows. PR-02's 17 x 12 x 3 cm size and 600 g weight are assumed. The VENUS_L01 chest welt has a 9 cm opening and a 13.5 cm bag and leaves 1.5 cm of glass showing; PR-01 is assumed at about 200 g, carried on stay tapes, lens end down.
Venus's three hand marks are locked by the director's ruling, as recorded in the casting bible. In every look both sleeves end 12 cm above the wrist bone, and the hand double carries the same marks.
Jean in SC15-SC16 and Venus in L02 each wear a skin-matched modesty garment that is never seen. The sheet stays at his waist through the SC16 roll, so no piece needs nudity.
The L02 hem numbers rest on assumed proportions for a 177 cm woman: the high point of the shoulder at about 145 cm and the top of the kneecap at about 51 cm. The fitter holds the standing mark.

There is no product (R2 stretch), so the hue rule is run against the story's two reds: the REC dot #D7261E (approx L*47, C*82, h 37°) and the dried drops #6E1C18 (approx L*24, C*43, h 34°). Every garment in frame with them is either under C* 15 or far off in hue. Skin and hair are excluded, because skin is never altered.

One garment per look is older than the story, each with a rebuild method: Venus's pistol-worn back pocket and her L02 tee, Jean's belt, the bartender's apron, and the driver's sun-faded shirt (taste note: one real detail per scene).

Taste notes followed: hands before faces (every acting hand is bare, with cuffs at mid-forearm or above) and restraint over explanation (no symbolic jewellery; her whites and his black carry the verified colour theme). One craft rule is broken on purpose: VENUS_L02 stays inside the white room's palette so that Jean is the only dark mass.
I did not inspect any reference image, because no reference_reader is bound. The references are used only as the brief describes them, and no character is modelled on a face in them.

blockers.issue: The world bible I was given contradicts the film director's PR-04 ruling (quoted in the assumptions). It reads as follows. PR-04 S0, SC04-SC14: 'hooked by the left arm in Jean's placket over the fastened second button, held with a clear thread tack'. PR-04 S1 and PR-55 S2, SC15: 'folded, lenses up, on top of his folded shirt'. PR-04 S2, SC17: 'taken from that pile'. PR-56 S0-S2 and the LOC-05 description: 'PR-04 hooked in his placket'. PR-05: 'No outside pocket'. The director reports that the placket version has also reached the K08 kit sheet that drives every Jean print on the V01/S02 wall. Under the ruling one plant is lost. The world bible had the glasses on Jean alive, seen through the bar window in SC04, which tied PR-04 to him before V01. In story order they now first appear when she takes them out of his duffel in SC17. That loss is the director's to rule on. I have not restored it: there are no sunglasses in any K08 print.
blockers.responsible_agent: Production designer (world bible); film director (K08 kit sheet and the lost plant)
blockers.resolution: Production design: set PR-04 S0 (SC04-SC16) to PR-05's outside pocket; S1 (SC17) taken out of that pocket and put on his face before she zips the duffel. Give PR-05 its outside pocket; size and side are production design's call. Delete PR-04 from PR-55 S2, PR-56 S0-S2 and LOC-05, and add to PR-56: 'Nothing hangs from the shirt placket in SC04-SC15.' Film director: regenerate K08 from the JEAN_L01 rail (K08-A/B/C), with the placket bare in every print. Also rule whether the lost plant needs a replacement. One option, not applied here: PR-04 on his face in some K08-B day prints.

blockers.issue: Jean's double for the SH14 and SH19 plates has not been cast, so wardrobe can't fit SH-2 at C3 on him, and hair can't decide between cutting his own 4A hair and building the custom topper, which needs build time.
blockers.resolution: Casting supplies the double and books him a fitting. Hair cuts his own 4A hair to spec or builds the topper. Wardrobe fits SH-2 at C3 (or cuts him his own SH-2 from the same cloth). Wardrobe and hair sign off side by side with CHR-JEAN-DEAD@v1.

blockers.issue: Two pocket carries still need the prop owner's sign-off. (a) PR-02 rides slide down on a drill sling 6 cm inside the right back pocket, grip up at the side-seam end, muzzle toward the centre back, 6 cm of grip showing; its 17 x 12 x 3 cm size and about 600 g weight are assumed. (b) PR-01 rides lens end down in the jacket's chest welt, but PR-01 S2 says only 'screen-in'.
blockers.resolution: Confirm PR-02's orientation and weight in S1 and S3, adding 'slide down on the pocket sling, grip at the side-seam end'. Add 'lens end down' to PR-01 S2. If the prop comes in heavier or taller, wardrobe moves the sling fold so that 6 cm of grip still shows.

blockers.issue: Two blocking points follow from the looks and aren't in the script yet. (a) SC17: Venus changes off screen from the tee (L02) into the pressed shirt (L03), after the straw goes into PR-60 and before she closes the tin, washing off the kohl and putting her hair up. (b) SC18: wardrobe needs the elastics out and her hair down while she stands, and PR-01 out of the right front pocket before she sits.
blockers.resolution: Cut away for the SC17 change (the finished-room frame can cover it) and bring her back in L03 to close the tin. Set the SC18 order and tell wardrobe.

blockers.issue: Lucas's 'oversized Raptors t shirt' has lost its team. The L02 tee reads as an athletic shirt by its raglan cut and V-notch, but no team, city or colour can be shown until A10 clears the real shirt or a fictional team is designed and cleared.
blockers.responsible_agent: Lucas (creative lead) via producer, with production designer
blockers.resolution: Lucas chooses: accept the unmarked athletic tee, or have production design create a fictional team for the producer to clear under A10. If team colours come in, wardrobe re-runs the white-room rule break, because a saturated or dark team colour would put a second dark mass beside Jean.

evidence.specificity: All six earlier notes are fixed, and the page now leaves wardrobe, generation and the camera nothing to ask about. The K08 wall is now a rail someone can shoot from: 'K08-B, about 100 prints (40%), June to August day prints at the pump and crossing streets: a black heavyweight crew tee, sleeves to mid-bicep, worn untucked over TR-1, black socks, PR-41' and 'K08-C ... brushed cotton drill 300 g/m², solid, blue-black #292B30 (approx L*17)'. The third-night state can be checked in one frame and rebuilt: 'The collar points have gone soft, tips lifted 6-8 mm off the shirt front; horizontal crumple creases at both inner elbows; a fan of sit creases across the trouser lap ... the actor sits in SH-1 and TR-1 for 40 minutes with his elbows bent before the first take.' The car lock now covers only what the frame can see: '[car wide V01 34-42 s, and S01 from behind her right shoulder; everything above the 72 cm door line] White shirt, collar open to the third button ...'. It falls short of 10 only because the L03 underlayers are missing (see notes).
evidence.distinctiveness: The clothes tell this story and could not be moved to another project. 'The fastened top button is the change the camera sees: it sits at the collar her hand straightens in V01-B02, and he would never have done it himself.' 'Older than the story: the right back pocket is faded to #A9B9C9 in an L, the outline of the part of PR-02 that rides inside it.' 'A deep crease with cracked grain at the middle (third) hole, where it fastened before he got heavier.' The K08 variants date the wall across months ('Everything he is ever photographed in is black'). The next man is 'one suit, bought off the rack for court, a size loose', grey over white, so the wall visibly moves on to someone else.
evidence.fit: Lucas's idea shows in every look, and it is sharper than he wrote it. The white theme and the black hole are handled as a deliberate, flagged rule break: 'Both tones sit 5-14 L* under the walls #F4F2EE ... so she belongs to the white room ... and JEAN stays the only dark mass (verified: "The colour theme is white"; tone: clean).' His Raptors shirt survives as a shape, with the brand held back: 'Which team (Lucas's Raptors shirt) stays open until A10 clears it or a fictional team is designed and cleared.' 'No underwear' is implied and never shown, using modesty garments. The route's '#F2EEE6 her white shirt' is used as given, and '#111111' is kept as the graded read. The next man is kept fictional: 'matching no real person or case'. The PR-04 conflict is quoted and passed to its owners without being resolved on wardrobe's authority.
evidence.craft: This is now technique a senior stylist would sign. There are multiples for each state: 'SH-3, the dust repeat: identical to SH-2, pre-dusted to C1 ... so every brush take starts from C1 while SH-2 holds its later state'. 'SH-4, the dressing double: ... a centre-back split ... never in V01 0-56 s, where the phone sees the back of his collar.' Stain risk is named and covered: 'A second tee, aged the same way, stands by for SC17.' The separation risk on the bar set is stated honestly: 'Value alone won't separate him from the counter ... The rest is the DP's.' The cross-references are now quoted and sourced: 'It was issued by the film director in the package review ... the note carries no date.' The scope creep has been cut back to 'the order is the director's.' Three first-read catches keep it from 9. L03 lists no bra or briefs under white poplin open to the sternum. SH-2 has to be clean in SC17 and dusty in V01, although 'The nap holds PR-57's dust'. The L02 fold-crease positions don't match PR-55's 30 x 30 fold.

At the fitting, fold SH-1 to PR-55's square, measure where each crease lands on the front, and write those numbers into SH-2, SH-3 and SH-4 and into the lock. cues.description: Inside the phone. From frame 1, open-car wind hits a single phone mic, and the limiter pumps and clips on every gust. Under it are the small engine at cruise and the tires slapping road seams. Off screen, one loose shop awning flaps at f20 (0.83 s, sound-led), before her voice. Absent: traffic, voices, dogs and any car stereo, because the town is empty. Her laugh runs f43-f81 (SND-V01-015). Native audio on every generated clip is muted.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production. Wind and engine are captured on a phone mic held at arm's length in a hired vintage open two-seater at road speed, on an empty road, with no third-party voices. Scope: all media, worldwide, in perpetuity from first use, for V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot; owned by the production. The vehicle-hire and location agreements must allow recording, and no make is identified. Status: required, pending. Next step: the producer books the car and the recordist.

cues.timing: V01-B02, 4.0-10.0 s (f96-f240); strokes f132-f160, pinch f161-f185, pull-away f214 (CP)
cues.description: Hard cut at f96 onto the car braking. The wind halves and is gone by f115 (4.79 s), when the car settles on its springs with a small creak. From there the idle runs a little lumpy. Off screen, a tin sign creaks once on its chain at f120 (5.0 s, sound-led), before the hand. Her fingertips brush dust off his black cotton shirt close to the mic: stroke 1 f132-f145, stroke 2 f147-f160, each on its hand pass. On the pinch at f161 (6.71 s) the collar point creases dry, and it is pressed flat by f185 (7.71 s). Jean makes no sound. The clutch takes up and the engine pulls away on the SH03 lurch at f214 (8.92 s), and the wind is back on the mic by f229 (9.54 s). Picture-led, ±2. V02-SH01 is cut from 5.5-7.0 s. Fallback, if her hand only rests on his collar: one fabric touch on the landing frame, with no strokes and no press.

The sign creak is recorded on location, or licensed non-exclusively from a library: all media, worldwide, in perpetuity from first use (or the term the producer sets), for V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot. Status: required, pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: The wind roar cuts hard on the same frame as each picture cut. f240 (10.0 s, REC 00:21:40): the town, the wind bouncing off storefronts. f302 (12.58 s, 00:38:15): open desert, broad and even. f367 (15.29 s, 00:52:30): scrub hills, gusty, with the limiter clamping hard. Each cut lands on a fresh snatch of her laugh (SND-V01-015). f367-f432 is the loudest stretch in V01. No whoosh and no riser: the roar is the cut. V02-SH02 is cut from f367.

cues.description: Wind on the mic, with a little less roar in the lower sun. Her thumb on the glass is loud because the mic sits right beside it. It squeaks across to the flip icon f451-f475 (18.79-19.79 s) and makes a small pressure knock in the phone body as it settles at f475. It rests with only wind under it, then slides away f528-f547 (22.0-22.79 s). The icon makes no UI sound. Her shorter laugh comes on the frame shake after the thumb clears (target f559, 23.29 s). Picture-led, ±2. Fallback, the under-a-second flip: a 2-frame audio dropout at the flip and again at the flip back, with no camera sound.

cues.description: Hard cut at f624 to blue dusk. The wind on the mic eases as the car slows, and tires on grit come up underneath. At f689 (28.71 s) a small side-button click sounds, dull and loud through the phone body. It is off screen, because we are inside the phone. The video light comes on at f696 (29.0 s) with no sound of its own, and the glint on his collar gets none either: no hum, drone or sting. At f754 (31.42 s), the SH10 road-bump join, the front tire thuds over a break in the tarmac, felt through the chassis, and the phone knocks in her grip, giving a handling bump on the mic. The bump carries the join, so the take reads as unbroken. No laugh in this beat. Picture-led, ±2.

cues.type: atmos, perspective switch (phone mic to 35mm exterior)
cues.description: f816-f835: wind on the phone mic, with a handling bump at f829-f835 as her grip shifts. At f835, the frame where the picture widens to 35mm, the phone mic cuts and we hear the world from outside the car. The wind drops away, and the two-seater's engine and tires on grit come from a roadside position, with a light breeze in dry creosote. Absent: birds, insects and any other engine. This is the first clean, quiet sound in V01, and its cleanness against the phone's clipping is what the switch sounds like. No projector whirr or optical crackle: the film look is picture only. One continuous laugh runs over it from f835 (SND-V01-015). Picture-led: the switch shares the widen's frame.

cues.timing: V01-B07, 42.0-50.0 s (f1008-f1200); sunglasses f1032; headrest creak f1080, turn to f1114
cues.description: A closer perspective, with the engine and tires low. The arm of his sunglasses slides out of his hair with a dry scratch on the lift (target f1032, 43.0 s, inside V02-SH03's source f1027-f1051). His cheek leaves the leather headrest with a short creak on the first frame of the chin turn, f1080 (45.0 s), and his collar shifts through the turn to f1114 (46.42 s). f1114-f1200 holds on the eyes. The only sound near him is his black cotton collar fluttering against his neck, soft and close, over the low engine. No laugh, no breath, no sting and no drone: this is the quietest moment of the drive, and the missing laugh is the reveal. Picture-led, ±2. Fallback A16 (car parked): the same foley with the engine off, and cooling ticks in place of the tires.

cues.timing: V01-B11, 64.0-72.0 s (f1536-f1728); trunk f1538-f1552; his bag f1555, her bag f1582, sacks f1606-f1632; SH22 shoves f1668 and f1692, door stop f1704; bag drop f1710-f1727 (CP), thud f1718

Unload in picture order: his black canvas duffel dragged over the trunk lip at f1555 (64.79 s), a dry canvas scuff and a dull weight; her bag at f1582 (65.92 s); two paper grocery sacks crackling, with cans shifting inside, f1606-f1632 (66.92-68.0 s). The second (target f1692, 70.5 s) is a harder thump, then the door scrapes open over grit, swings to 90° and knocks against its stop (target f1704, 71.0 s), the knock B13 hears again. She exits into the dark. Off screen, in the dark, f1710-f1727: the canvas strap slithers off her shoulder and the duffel thuds onto bare boards (landing f1718, 71.58 s, sound-led), and its contents settle by f1727. cues.timing: V01-B12, 72.0-82.0 s (f1728-f1968); lantern f1747; SH23 printer f1752-f1773, cans f1774-f1809, oranges f1810-f1821, jugs f1822-f1843, sacks slide f1863-f1877; SH24 chair f1878-f1899, boots f1938-f1967
cues.description: Hard cut inside, into the dark. The door stands open at 90° from here to the end, so the room isn't sealed. The wind comes straight in through the doorway, the dry palms and the sign's loose panel are faint outside, and the tin roof ticks as it cools. Absent: any hum, fridge or buzz, because there is no power. In the dark, the paper sacks are set on the table and crackle (f1730-f1742, T, sound-led). The lantern's plastic switch clicks at f1747 (72.79 s), and the light comes up to f1762 with no sound of its own. SH23, her hands in picture order: the printer is lifted out and set down, hollow plastic on wood, f1752-f1773. Three pairs of cans are set down on wood, f1774-f1785, f1786-f1797 and f1798-f1809, each pair a doubled knock a frame apart on its contact. The oranges land in soft thuds, f1810-f1821. Two full water jugs land, the water slapping and settling, f1822-f1843. The emptied paper sacks slide off the table edge with a dry paper slide and a light crumple on the floor, f1863-f1877. SH24: the second chair's leg drags across the boards f1878-f1899 (78.25-79.13 s) and settles. Then her boots cross the bare boards as she walks past the lens, f1938-f1967 (80.75-81.96 s), the boards giving under each step: close, then gone. Between hits there is only the room and the wind. Picture-led, ±2.

cues.timing: V01-B13, 82.0-88.0 s (f1968-f2112); door knocks its stop at f2006 and f2069
cues.description: A held frame. Nothing in the room moves, so nothing in the room is heard. The wind comes straight in through the open doorway, not muffled, and works the open door behind camera. As each gust swells, the swollen hinges groan, and then the door knocks against its stop at f2006 and f2069 (83.58 and 86.21 s): the same knock as SH22's f1704. The last gust has died by f2107 (87.79 s), and the room's own air runs underneath. Sound-led: the door is out of frame and the picture is still, so nothing has to hit these knocks.

cues.description: The laugh is Venus's only voice in V01 (A15), and Jean makes no sound, not even breath. B01: loud and right on the mic. Its onset is on the SH01 jolt at f43, and it runs to f81 so it covers every jolt. B03: a different snatch on each roar cut. B04: shorter. B06: one continuous laugh from the widen at f835, further off in SH12 and closer in SH13, with no break at the cut, and the tail gone by f1007 so none carries into B07. B06 plays as sync in both shots, because at 4.5 m SH12 shows her whole laughing face and torso. The actor records it while watching SH12 and SH13 cut together (f835-f1007), and every peak sits within 2 frames of a visible torso shake in both shots. The picture is generated without speech; if the mouth won't sit, do a lip-sync pass with the same consented recording. B08: softer and close, over before the thumb at f1272. No laugh in B07. B01, B03, B04 and B08 are off-mouth, because she is behind the phone. Read: aimed at him, as if he's in on the joke; delight, not mania; never a villain's laugh or a horror cue. Keep it off the fallback flips' face frames.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production with the actor cast as Venus (not yet cast), who is the one voice for Venus across V01, V02 and the pilot. Her written consent is required for V01, V02 (organic and paid social, and the pitch-deck embed) and the pilot: all media, worldwide, with the term from first use set by the producer. It must allow takes to be edited and resequenced, and must exclude synthetic cloning or model training without separate written consent. No library or AI-generated laugh. Status: required, pending. Owner: producer.

cues.type: music: none (by design), plus the sound arc
cues.description: No score and no temp track in any cut (route R2; tone: music; taste note: sound design before music). The wind, her laugh and the room carry it. Native clip audio is muted, and no generated audio is used. The arc: the loudest stretch is f367-f432 (15.29-18.0 s), the scrub-hills roar. The f754 road bump is a transient, not a peak. The big drop comes at f835 (34.79 s): the phone comes down, the clipping stops, and we hear the world as it is. The quietest living stretch is f1114-f1200 (46.42-50.0 s), on the eyes. In the room, one hand-made sound plays at a time, with the wind through the open door between them. Digital silence runs f2112-f2160 under the title. The 35mm look adds no sound.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: None while no music is used. No temp track may be cut in, even for internal use. Any track proposed later needs its own cue with a source and scope; a commercial track needs sync rights for all the publishing plus the master. Generated audio is excluded, because it carries no promise of ownership or exclusivity.

cues.description: Re-cut from the V01-B02 recordings at the picture's in-point, V01 5.5 s, so each hit keeps its V01 frame.
